store_data.about_the_game:
Hubert catching is a fun and simple game where you desperately scramble to throw small living stone pingies (penguins) into a hole, in an attempt to appease the beings that sent you into this realm so they may eventually set you free. Little do you know, your purpose is greater than a simple game.

The task is simple: grab up to 2 Huberts (living stone figures which are also somehow a penguin species) at a time, and then throw them into a hole. Once you have collected 10 Huberts, your time will be recorded and you will be sent back to the main menu. From there you can purchase upgrades and one-time consumables to assist you in achieving a faster time. However the more you play the more you realize that your purpose here was for much more than just simple entertainment.

Content included in the game:

  • A simple catching game where you must grab one moving Hubert at a time in each hand, using left and right click to grab them.

  • A credit system based on your time in each round, where you gain more money based on how fast you win.

  • Consumables which can be bought in the shop and used once in a round before being removed from your inventory.

  • Upgrades which can replace/modify your hands (don’t think too hard about it) to change the method in which you collect Huberts.

  •  A Speedrun Timer and in-game Leaderboard.

(despite how the description may sound, the game does not actually cover most of the story elements. Unless.. Maybe if you get a good enough score… maybe then something will happen? COMING SOON)

store_data.about_the_game:
DESCEND, FOR THE LIGHT ABOVE HAS FORSAKEN YOU

EMBER is a dark cinematic 2.5D platformer set within a beautiful and merciless world.

Descend through a procession of handcrafted places, where every chamber bears its own trial, every mechanism conceals its purpose, and every living thing hungers for your end.

There shall be no safe road beneath your feet.
There shall be no mercy in the jaws of the deep.
There shall be only the path before you—and the sorrow that follows behind.

LET EVERY STEP BE MEASURED

Movement is your only prayer.

Responsive controls and strict timing make every jump, landing, and reaction matter. Read the shape of the world, learn the rhythm of its machinery, and place each step with care.

For the careless shall fall.
And the hesitant shall be taken.

DEATH COMES IN A SINGLE TOUCH

There are no wounds to endure and no second chances to spend.

Traps and creatures kill in a single hit. Observe what destroyed you. Remember what the darkness revealed. Return wiser than before—and perish better, should wisdom fail you.

GO DOWN, AND BEHOLD WHAT WAS BURIED

Descend through a focused sequence of handcrafted locations, each introducing new hazards, creatures, and mechanics.

Old signs speak through dying projectors. Bells burn like sacred lanterns and mark the places to which the fallen may return. Forgotten machines stir beneath the earth, obeying laws written long before your coming.

The deeper you go, the less the world remembers the light.

THE SCRIPTURE OF THE DEEP

  • Precise and responsive platforming

  • Death from a single hit

  • Handcrafted, linear locations

  • New hazards and mechanics throughout the descent

  • Hostile creatures and grotesque encounters

  • Cinematic 2.5D presentation

  • Hand-drawn animation and a stylized dark world

  • Keyboard and controller support

And the light gave life unto all things.



Yet beneath the earth, even light learned to hunger.

store_data.about_the_game:
A TRUE CRIME SIMULATOR — VOLUME I

You are Detective Partridge, investigating the disappearance of a missing girl at a run-down trailer park at the end of a gravel road. Piece together the mystery of what happened to Abbey Pullman by cross-examining the residents of the trailer park and searching for clues.

TALK LIKE A DETECTIVE

Type your own questions. Investigate how you want. There are NO dialogue trees. What they will tell you, what they will deny, and what they emotionally cannot face yet are all subject to change. Push them with evidence you find, or inconsistencies in their stories. Watch composure crack or earn trust.

They do not recite scripts. They hold secrets. And they will not say what they do not know. Investigate the crime by asking the characters ANYTHING you want, just like a real detective. 

INVESTIGATE LIKE IT MATTERS

The environment of the trailer park holds secrets to discover just as much as the characters do. Learn as much as you can to confront the characters with evidence and expose the truth of what happened to Abbey Pullman. 

THE SUSPECTS:

Chuck Pullman: a father who will not leave his campfire until his daughter comes home. 

Daisy Brichard: the sweetest grandmother imaginable, baking for when Abby gets back. 

Desmond Lloyd: a paranoid man nobody believes. He may be right about everything.

Made by Morph

.

Note: This game contains generative AI in the form of NPCs being able to respond to the user's actual input and questions. The game loads a local, offline, LLM (Llama 3.1 8B), and when you interact with the NPC characters, there is a combination of code architecture and LLM interaction that makes each response unique and perfectly in line with story lore. Generative AI was not used to create the game, but is used as a gameplay mechanic.

store_data.about_the_game:
One board. Four players. No mercy.

Breaker League is a competitive falling-block puzzler with a twist: everyone shares the SAME board. Your zone is yours to build, until a rival drops a piece right into it. Steal space, sabotage setups, and detonate chains across the whole field while three other players try to do the same to you.

Fight dirty with Specials

Before every match, arm yourself with one of 12 special tiles that completely change how you play. The Bob-omb detonates when surrounded, clearing all 8 neighbors. The Axe destroys an entire column on landing. The Ink Bomb coats nearby tiles so nobody can see their color. The UFO abducts every tile of one color and pockets the points. The 8-Ball scatters surrounding tiles like a pool break. Plus Dynamite, Bowling Pin, Salamander, Painter's Palette, Mushroom, Padlock, and the Microphone mic-drop.

A veritable Wack-Pack of Unlockable Characters

Play as one of 37 fighters, including Apple Bear, Banana Duck, A Literal Shrimp, Biblically Accurate Cake, a Dumpster, a Yellow Cab, and The Sun itself. Unlock them all through the campaign.

Story Mode

Battle through a 32-level campaign spanning sun-soaked orchards, erupting volcanoes, the edge of the void, neon city streets, a high-stakes gambling bar, one very rowdy concert, and beyond. Face boss arenas, survive gauntlet worlds where your health carries from fight to fight, and unlock new characters and specials along the way.

Customizable Local & Online Multiplayer

Points: first to the target score wins. Health: combos deal damage, last one standing takes it. Showdown: 1v1 sudden death on twin columns, double points, no room for error. Timed: highest score when the clock hits zero. Dial in stage hazards, minimum chain size, and grid layouts. Play solo against CPUs, grab up to 4 controllers for couch chaos, or take it online and grind up your global ranking.

Features

Shared-board competitive puzzle action for 1–4 players. Online multiplayer via Steam. 4-player local versus with drop-in controllers. 32-level story campaign with cutscenes, bosses, and unlocks. 37 playable characters and 12 special tiles. 13 stage themes with toggle-able hazards.

The Axe destroys an entire column on landing. The Ink Bomb coats nearby tiles so nobody can see their color. The UFO abducts every tile of one color and pockets the points. The 8-Ball scatters surrounding tiles like a pool break. Plus Dynamite, Bowling Pin, Salamander, Painter's Palette, Mushroom, Padlock, and the Microphone mic-drop.

A veritable Wack-Pack of Unlockable Characters

Play as one of 37 fighters, including Apple Bear, Banana Duck, A Literal Shrimp, Biblically Accurate Cake, a Dumpster, a Yellow Cab, and The Sun itself. Unlock them all through the campaign.

Story Mode

Battle through a 32-level campaign spanning sun-soaked orchards, erupting volcanoes, the edge of the void, neon city streets, a high-stakes gambling bar, one very rowdy concert, and beyond. Face boss arenas, survive gauntlet worlds where your health carries from fight to fight, and unlock new characters and specials along the way.

Customizable Local & Online Multiplayer

Points: first to the target score wins. Health: combos deal damage, last one standing takes it. Showdown: 1v1 sudden death on twin columns, double points, no room for error. Timed: highest score when the clock hits zero. Dial in stage hazards, minimum chain size, and grid layouts. Play solo against CPUs, grab up to 4 controllers for couch chaos, or take it online and grind up your global ranking.

Features

Shared-board competitive puzzle action for 1–4 players. Online multiplayer via Steam. 4-player local versus with drop-in controllers. 32-level story campaign with cutscenes, bosses, and unlocks. 37 playable characters and 12 special tiles. 13 stage themes with toggle-able hazards.
store_data.short_description: Puzzle-battle mayhem on one shared board. Drop pieces, chain combos, and invade your rivals' turf in frantic 1–4 player matches online or on the couch. 37 ridiculous fighters, 12 game-changing specials, and a 32-level story campaign.

store_data.about_the_game:
The world has already fallen.

As one of Earth’s last surviving defenders, you walk alone across an endless, desolate bridge toward the inner city. Towering, extradimensional anomalies block the path ahead. There are no backup forces, no leveling systems, and no conventional weapons. Your only tool for survival is flawless defensive execution.

Turn their bullets against them.

This is not a traditional hack-and-slash platformer. You cannot button-mash your way through the swarm. Instead, you must navigate dense bullet hell barrages and master a unique, high-stakes parry system. By deflecting incoming strikes and projectiles with frame-perfect timing, you transform the enemy's overwhelming offensive firepower into your own lethal counterattacks.

Key Features

  • Abandon traditional attack button spam. Master a precise, defensive parry system to carve through bullet hell patterns and dismantle massive extradimensional threats.

  • A dark, highly stylized black-and-white visual presentation designed for maximum contrast, readability, and atmospheric isolation.

  • Built around a linear, perfectly balanced difficulty curve. There is no artificial stat grinding or luck—victory is earned entirely through pattern recognition and mechanical mastery.

  • This demo slice pits you against two distinct, multi-phase horrors: the relentless Orum, and Megalo Aza—a colossal, face-stealing dragon serpent.

  • Features first-class, highly responsive controller support engineered from the ground up for tight platforming and frame-perfect deflections.

store_data.about_the_game:
The house always wins — so become the house.

The Rouge Casino is a score-attack roguelite deckbuilder, played across eight complete casino games that share one crooked spine: climb eight antes of Small, Big and Boss blinds, cash out, and spend it all in a shop that sells you ways to cheat. Every table has its own deck to build — you don't just play the wheel, the dice, the reels. You rig them.

THE EIGHT TABLES

  • Roulette Rouge — bet the wheel you built. Remove pockets, load the ball, nudge it after it lands.

  • Blackjack Noir — beat a house that cheats first. Strip the shoe, dye the suits, stack the count.

  • Slot Syndicate — rig your own machine. Rewrite the reel strips symbol by symbol.

  • Craps Crimson — carve the dice, chase the point. Re-pip the faces themselves.

  • Bingo Baroque — one card, daubed to the bone. Cull the cage until your numbers must fall.

  • Darts & Deals — a quiver of crooked arrows. Renumber the board, widen the beds.

  • Domino Dynasty — build the line, hit the fives. Forge duplicate bones, whittle the deadweight.

  • Mahjong Méchant — a wicked wall, a perfect hand. Sweep the junk tiles, smith extra dragons.

THE RUN Beat the target score or lose the run. Boss blinds twist the rules every ante; every eighth ante belongs to a finisher — The House Always Wins, or The Final Audit. Skip a blind for one of 16 tags, level your scoring events with Markers, and spend your winnings on charms, omens, vouchers and booster packs while interest ticks on every $5 you refuse to spend.

THE CHEATING Stamp your own objects — cards, pockets, faces, symbols, balls, wedges, bones, tiles — with enhancements and seals: Gilded, Crimson, Mirrored, Champagne, Bronze reserves, Lucky, Loaded, Wild; Gold, Scarlet, Cobalt, Violet. Shop charms roll Argent, Mirage, Prismatic and Void editions. Every system works in every game.

THE LONG GAME

  • 8 stakes per table, from Ivory to the Rouge Stake — the top tiers add Eternal, Perishable and Rental charms

  • 6 table variants per game and 10 challenges per table (80 in all), each with a persistent ✦ badge

  • Endless mode past Ante 8, where the targets climb without mercy

  • A discovery Collection that fills as you meet the house's charms, omens and bosses — nothing gated, everything earned

  • Seeded runs: copy any run's seed with one click and share the exact same casino with a friend

  • Jacques, the croupier, who explains every table and judges you gently

AT YOUR TABLE, YOUR WAY Full controller and Steam Deck-style navigation, colorblind-safe palette, screen-shake toggle, UI scaling, and separate music/SFX sliders.

HONEST ABOUT THE DISHONESTY The Rouge Casino contains no real-money gambling of any kind — no wagering, no purchasable currency, no microtransactions, no loot boxes. It's a single-purchase game about fictional chips and the fine art of cheating a fictional house.

store_data.about_the_game:
Nobody asked for another chess game.

We made one anyway.

Last Gambit is a chess-themed roguelike. Yes, one of those games that claim to reinvent a timeless classic. Don't worry: we failed. It just adds enough chaos to make twenty years of opening theory useless and to make you miss regular chess.

Oh, and it's free to play, so the only thing you lose is your time.

What's inside


27 pieces or more, from the classics to the ones a chess purist would report to the authorities: the Unicorn, the Griffon, the Void Queen (walks off one edge, comes back on the other, good luck defending), the Phoenix (dies, is reborn, goes back to bothering you), Catapults and Trebuchets that launch pieces, the Summoner, the Mirror.

Free deployment: no mandatory formation. Place your pieces however you like, then regret it.

Fusions and evolutions: combine pieces to create new ones. The Knight can become a Unicorn, Bishop and Knight fuse into an Archbishop. The recipe table is more complicated than it needs to be. We noticed too late.

Story Mode, a branching map in the Slay the Spire style: chapters full of levels, a boss to close them out, battles, merchants, perks to collect (rewind, teleport, freeze, and others that feel like cheats because they sort of are).

Real cross-play, across everything: a central server, unified matchmaking. PC versus Android, the exact same 1v1 match.

Cosmetic skins you unlock by playing, to at least give the impression that you know what you're doing.

Play offline whenever you want. Online is only there if you feel like challenging real people (not recommended for your self-esteem).

store_data.about_the_game:
Lo-Fi with Ruka is a quiet rainy-night study room designed to help you finish what matters, one session at a time.

Write down a goal, choose a 25, 45, or 60-minute focus session, and settle into a looping animated room with lo-fi music. Completed sessions, goals, and focus time build a calendar that helps you review your rhythm over time.

Focus and music

  • 25, 45, and 60-minute focus presets
  • 50 built-in lo-fi tracks with non-repeating shuffle
  • Local MP3, OGG, and WAV music import
  • Playlists, favorites, previous-track control, fades, and normalized loudness
  • Immersive mode and fullscreen controls

Optional companionship from Ruka

AI companionship is text-first. With your own DeepSeek API key, Ruka can reply to short messages and continue a personal study-room story connected to your progress. With your own StepFun API key, generated replies can be read aloud. Both services are optional, and their keys remain on your device.

Ruka keeps only a bounded memory of recent goals, completion outcomes, and selected non-sensitive preferences. You can clear this companion memory at any time without deleting your focus calendar.

Quiet Steam companionship

When Steam is available, focus progress can sync through Steam Cloud. You can see friends who are focusing, exchange preset notes, and invite up to eight participants into a friends-only group for a synchronized 25-minute session. There is no real-time chat.

Native support is included for Windows 64-bit, Intel Mac, and Apple silicon Mac.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to the Dream Post Office

You play as Anna, a young woman who has lost all memory of her life before joining the company. Seated before an employee terminal that looks as though it came from the end of the last century, you receive orders, verify records, write incantations, and piece together scattered dream fragments to create the dream each client truly needs.

Investigate the post office and reply to coworkers during the day. Choose between dream orders and personal invitations in the evening. Before night falls, do not forget to finish your work—the Dream Post Office has little patience for underperforming employees.

At first, it all seems like ordinary employee training.

Until Anna receives a letter addressed to herself.

The sender is Anna. The recipient is also Anna.

Deliver Each Dream to the Right Person

Every order contains a story that was never properly told.

Access the central archives and use the client’s information to identify the true recipient. Enter an incantation to step into their consciousness, listen to the feelings they have kept hidden, and select the correct combination from dream fragments where truth and falsehood are intertwined.

A rainstorm, a test paper marked zero, a lighthouse that never lit up, or a letter that arrived ten years too late—dreams may not be able to rewrite the past, but perhaps they can help someone see what was once overlooked.

Choosing the wrong fragments will not immediately end the story. You may still deliver the dream, but a wish forced into the wrong shape may become something else entirely, affecting both the order rating and the post office’s attitude toward you.

Work, Life, and the Weekly Performance Review

Each day at the Dream Post Office is divided into daytime, evening, and late night. You can investigate unusual files, chat with coworkers, accept invitations to meet, or complete one of the three dream orders available that day.

But there is never enough time.

Going to an appointment may mean missing work, while focusing entirely on work may cause you to miss other stories. At the end of each week, the post office will evaluate your performance. Fail the review, and the entire week will be declared invalid, sending time back to Monday.

Everyone else forgets the failed week.

You may still remember it.

Meet Seven Coworkers from Different Eras

A sharp-eyed sorter with a stubborn streak, a performance clerk terrified of disappointing others, a systems technician from the age of early computers, and an elderly postman who has preserved countless unclaimed apologies…

Get to know the daily lives and pasts of seven coworkers through messages, casual conversations, gifts, invitations, and personal side stories. Restore hidden messages, listen to the echoes they refuse to speak about, and build friendships strong enough for secrets to be entrusted to one another.

They come from different eras, yet none of them remembers how they arrived here.

A “Real” Retro Computer Terminal

The employee desktop is more than a menu—it is the equipment Anna uses for her work every day.

Messages, notes, contacts, the supply shop, corrupted files, and even the seemingly insignificant Recycle Bin may all be part of the story. As the investigation into the post office deepens, the familiar desktop will gradually reveal files and records that should not exist.

Beyond the retro office system, each dream is presented through softly colored, hand-drawn illustrations. Quiet buildings, gentle tones, and surreal imagery intertwine to reveal the tender yet unsettling other side of the Dream Post Office.

Investigate a Letter Addressed to Yourself

The address in the letter does not exist on any map.

Anna’s employee records have been overwritten.

The Recycle Bin still contains files that should have been permanently deleted.

While completing your work, follow fragmented recordings, activity logs, private emails, and employee memories to uncover your own past. Do not be too quick to trust the system’s conclusions—the post office is very good at extracting half of a sentence while ensuring that no one ever hears the rest.

Some promises are made in moments of absolute despair.

But a decision made in such a moment should never become a contract that no one can escape.

Game Features

  • An approximately 30-minute single-player narrative experience featuring a complete six-chapter main story and multiple coworker side stories

  • More than 100 unique dream orders

  • Verify recipients, enter incantations, combine dream fragments, and witness the results of each delivery

  • Every order includes both correct and incorrect dream outcomes

  • Schedule management across daytime, evening, and late night, plus performance reviews that can rewind an entire week

  • Seven coworkers, each with unique dialogue, invitations, relationships, and personal stories

  • A retro desktop system that weaves windows, notifications, permissions, corrupted files, and the Recycle Bin into the narrative

  • A dual visual style combining a retro operating-system interface with softly hand-drawn dreamscapes

  • A story about dreams, promises, and the journey home

store_data.about_the_game:
PURE MOMENTUM, HIGH AUTONOMY, UNSTOPPABLE ACTION

The floor is your enemy. Immerse yourself in a futuristic, vertical world drenched in vibrant neon lights. You command two distinct forces: a high-velocity Grappling Gun in one hand to swing through the skyline like an apex predator, and a devastating arsenal of weapons in the other to turn rogue robots into scrap metal. If you stop moving, you die. Keep your momentum, stay airborne, and find your flow!

Key Features:

  • Infinite Momentum & Fluid Movement: Master physics-based grappling mechanics to soar between platforms without losing speed. The ground is merely a pit stop—touch down for a split second to recharge your stamina, then launch yourself straight back into the stratosphere.

  • Hypnotic Neon Aesthetics & Stress Relief: Visually striking, non-intrusive neon environments combined with a rhythmic gameplay loop create the ultimate "flow state." It's intense, fast-paced action designed to let you blow off steam and shred enemies effortlessly.

  • Dynamic Card Draft System: Adapt and evolve on the fly. Choose from specialized upgrade cards every time you level up to boost your firepower, extend your grappling reach, or push your mobility past its limits. Craft the perfect build for every run!

  • Elite Skill Chests: Pulling the trigger isn't enough; you need to dominate. Reach specific kill milestones to unlock high-tier chests packed with game-changing active skills that will melt through enemy ranks.

The Gameplay Loop

  • Swing & Shoot: Staying airborne is your best defense. Line up your shots and blast mechanical threats while swinging mid-air.

  • Adapt & Evolve: Select strategic upgrade cards as you level up, combining passive traits into powerful combat combos.

  • Unleash the Chests: Fill your kill counter, unlock tactical skill chests, and watch the arena dissolve into neon sparks.

store_data.about_the_game:
Paradise Won’t Survive the Night

The outbreak began only hours ago.

Miami Beach still shines beneath the tropical sun, but the streets are empty, communications are dead, and something is hunting between the abandoned hotels, beaches, and neon-lit alleys.

In Death Paradise, you must survive the first 24 hours of a zombie catastrophe, assemble a team, restore the island’s emergency systems, and transmit an SOS signal before paradise falls completely.

You Have 24 Hours

The infection is spreading.

Daylight gives you time to search the island, recover supplies, rescue stranded survivors, and prepare vital infrastructure. But as evening approaches, the infected become more numerous and every objective becomes harder to complete.

Find the generator.

Restore power to the antennas.

Get the emergency signal online.

Then keep everything running long enough for rescue to find you.

Build Your Team

Not everyone escaped the first wave.

During the campaign, you will find and rescue three AI-controlled survivors. Each rescued teammate joins your squad and fights beside you in future missions.

Customize the appearance and beach outfits of your companions, equip yourself for the next mission, and keep your team alive as the situation becomes increasingly desperate.

Every survivor you save gives you another chance to make it through the night.

Weapon

Fight with firearms, bows, brutal melee weapons, and improvised equipment found throughout the island.

Cut through the infected with a katana, keep enemies at a distance with military rifles, or charge into danger using a trash-can lid as a makeshift shield.

Choose the right weapon for the situation—or use whatever is still in your hands.

They Don’t All Move Like Zombies

Some infected stumble toward you.

Others sprint, leap, spit acid, dodge gunfire, or explode when they get too close.

Each enemy type changes the rhythm of combat, forcing you to move, react, and adapt before your team is overwhelmed.

Survival Is More Than Killing

The island is collapsing, and bullets alone will not save you.

Restore generators, activate communication antennas, recover emergency equipment, rescue survivors, defend strategic locations, and hold back waves of infected while critical systems come online.

Your final objective is simple:

Keep the SOS signal active and reach the evacuation point before the island goes dark.

The Longest Day in Paradise

Gather your team.

Restore the signal.

Survive the first 24 hours.

Escape before paradise becomes a graveyard.

Don't just evade the oncoming enemies. Attack, block, and counter to take control of the fight.

Chain Your Moves and Crush the Horde

Chain your moves against the oncoming enemies, counter their attacks, and drive them all the way to the wall.

Land three consecutive Perfect Guards to stun every enemy on the battlefield.

Keep the Pressure On and Turn the Fight Around

Keep your offense going with air combos, combos against downed enemies, and wall combos.

Break out of danger and counterattack with a Guard Reversal or a Reversal after a perfectly timed dodge.

Combine Active Cards and Passives.

Combine Active Skill Cards with Passive Rewards to create a new fighting style every run.

Read Their Moves and Strike Back

    Read enemies that attack, charge, pressure you from range, or guard, then respond to each situation.

  • Active Skill Cards and Passive Builds

    Combine Active Skill Cards with Passive Rewards to create a new fighting style every run.

Read the enemy. Block. Dodge. Strike back.

store_data.about_the_game:
Wayfarer Protocol is a colony sim set on a single starship. You start with a cramped hull, a reactor that barely keeps up, and a crew that will suffocate, starve, or burn if you look away too long. Everything past that, you build.

Lay down floor and hull one tile at a time. Wire in reactors, oxygen recyclers, hydroponics, a kitchen, bunks. Bolt turrets and thrusters onto the outside of the hull. Every system pulls power and throws off heat, and a reactor that falls behind will brown out exactly the half of the ship you needed running.

Your crew aren't stat blocks. They get hungry, tired, and scared, and each one carries traits that cut both ways: a hard worker, a coward, a green thumb who doubles your harvests, a night owl who needs less sleep. Their morale sinks when the ship falls apart around them. When a fire breaks out or the hull cracks open to space, someone drops what they're doing to deal with it. If the breach is on the outside, they suit up and go out on a tether to patch it.

Then you jump. Every sector deals a fresh hand: an asteroid field worth stripping, a trader worth hailing, a distress call that might be a trap, pirates who will cut through your hull to take the cargo. You fight with whatever you bolted on: lasers, mass drivers, plasma, a railgun that guts one enemy system per shot. Fights are won by dropping their shields and picking apart their engines, guns, and life support before they do it to you.

Ten sectors deep, something far bigger is waiting for you. It doesn't take bribes.

Lose the whole crew and the run ends there. Get them through to the other side and you'll have earned it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Ready or not, here they come!

At the Large Hadron Collider, a team of physicists pushes an experiment a little too far and opens a portal into another dimension. Behold!  The Hedra come pouring through: hungry, bad-tempered, interdimensional polyhedral monsters led by rival Overlords. You are one of those Overlords! Seize the collider, complete your objectives, eat the physicists, and escape before the whole facility tears itself apart.

Hedra is the digital edition of an original physical board game developed and refined over ten years. It brings tile laying, dice combat, card play, unique spatial pattern building, and tactical movement to a board that grows differently every game.

The digital edition handles the setup, rules, bookkeeping, and CPU turns (your computer opponents are very, very nasty, btw...), leaving you to concentrate on the wonderfully strange puzzle spreading across the table.

Build the collider as you play

Place Room Tiles to expand the facility one piece at a time. Every placement changes the routes across the collider and may complete one of your Room Pattern cards. A completed pattern can score Victory Points or bring a new Hedra die onto the board, giving you an immediate choice between points and power.

The digital tile supply contains 216 Room Tiles:

  • 80 triangles, where new Hedra dice enter the collider

  • 80 squares, where physicists can be found and consumed

  • 28 hexagons, which supply Hedra Fight cards

  • 16 octagons, which reveal Hedra Effects

  • 10 dodecagons, which interact with Facility Effects

  • 2 icosagons, rare rooms capable of major upgrades

The shapes tessellate in unusual ways, so a promising pattern can emerge from a tiny gap, a long chain of rooms, or a tile your opponent placed for entirely different reasons. There are 72 Room Pattern cards to chase, ranging from compact arrangements to sprawling geometric projects.

Grow monsters. Eat scientists (Hedra love scientists... they're delicious!).

Your Hedra are represented by polyhedral dice: d4s, d6s, d8s, d12s, and d20s. Move them through the collider, consume physicists to grow into larger forms, and send them into rooms occupied by enemy Hedra.

Fights account for die size, current health, room effects, and the cards played during combat. The game includes 32 Hedra Fight cards, 32 Hedra Effect cards, and 32 Facility Effect cards, giving each match plenty of opportunities for clever timing and sudden trouble.

Every Overlord has a plan

Ten Hedra Overlord cards provide endgame goals tied to patterns, room shapes, and control of the collider. Your Overlord can turn an ordinary-looking position into a valuable long-term project, while the other Overlords pursue plans of their own.

Play solo against one to five computer-controlled rivals. CPU Overlords can use different strategic approaches, including pattern building, aggressive movement, immediate scoring, combat, Overlord objectives, and the dangerous rush for an icosagon.

Get out before it blows

Once an Overlord reaches the Victory Point threshold, the collider enters a self-destruct countdown. Everyone gets a few final turns to complete patterns, start fights, consume physicists, grab last-minute points, and reach the Lobby. The board starts coming apart. There is still time to win.

Features

  • Solo strategy play against one to five CPU Overlords

  • A shared board assembled from six different polygon shapes

  • 216 Room Tiles and 72 geometric Room Pattern cards

  • Polyhedral Hedra that grow from d4s into powerful d20s

  • Tile placement, tactical movement, card play, combat, and endgame objectives

  • Ten Overlord cards with their own scoring priorities

  • A 3D tabletop presentation with tabletop and overhead views

  • A guided tutorial, in-game rules reference, and save-and-resume support

  • Based on a physical board game refined over ten years

  • Second-place winner in the KublaCon Game Design Contest

This game is not available yet as an actual physical board game. I have a few copies of it that I've made. Maybe one day it will be. If you're an interested publisher, don't hesitate to reach out.

store_data.about_the_game:
In a world where magic is so rare it might as well not exist, most mages choose to hide their abilities and blend into normal society. Using magic openly is usually the trademark of criminals—or in this case, a desperate teenager. 

This game marks the very beginning of the group’s storyline, when Raymond (Ray), a 16-year-old secondary school student, is pushed to use magic in public under the direst of circumstances: getting his hands on the latest trending video game. (Un)fortunately for him, he gets caught red-handed by Freya, a 20-year-old university student.

Instead of calling the police, Freya and her cousin, Hunter, seize the opportunity to recruit Ray to the Spell Casting Crusaders. Despite the heroic name, their mission is to fulfill requests from the community for tips, only sometimes involving magic. And the entire rest of the group? Just Freya's younger brother, Fennix. 

Fulfill requests as both Freya and Ray, learning to integrate magic into your everyday life while navigating family secrets, personal grief, and the growing friction of a world.

Key Features

Mundane Requests, Magical Solutions: Play as both Freya and Ray as you use your magical abilities to fulfil ordinary requests. Combine items and magic in creative ways.

Interactive Narrative & Puzzles: Engage in a rich, dialogue-driven story featuring mini games, inventory combinations, and deductive puzzles.

A Grounded, Modern Magical World: Discover a unique, urban slice-of-life fantasy setting where magic is hereditary and monitored, but ultimately shaped by the personal resolve of those who wield it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build, explore, and transform a world where everything can be destroyed


In Terra Physics & money, every block is part of the world and can be removed, transported, used for construction, or sold. Dig through mountains, open new paths, and reshape the terrain as the environment reacts to your actions through a physics-based system.

A new experience every time you play


Each world is procedurally generated from a random seed. The terrain and resources change with every new journey, creating different opportunities, challenges, and building possibilities.

Millions of blocks in motion


Explore and reshape environments made of millions of blocks. The system was designed with performance in mind to keep the experience running smoothly, even as vast sections of the world are excavated and transformed.

Water, lava, and steam


Fluids are part of the simulation. Water and lava flow through the terrain, spread into new spaces, and can produce steam. Use these interactions to your advantage—or prepare to face the consequences of the changes you make to the environment.

Extract, build, and trade


Choose from a wide variety of building blocks to bring your ideas to life. Make use of the materials you uncover while exploring, expand your structures, and trade the blocks you extract to keep progressing.

Key features


  • A fully destructible world with physics-based behavior
  • Procedural generation from random seeds, making every playthrough unique
  • Millions of blocks in a system optimized to maintain a smooth frame rate
  • Fluid simulation, including water, lava, and steam
  • A wide variety of building blocks to choose from and use
  • Resource extraction and trading throughout the world
  • Fully translated into 10 languages from launch

Dig. Build. Trade. Transform the world—one block at a time.


[/p]

store_data.about_the_game:
Joust Your Friends

Jousting Around is an online multiplayer jousting game with a focus on fun, physics-based interactions. Jump into a medieval world as a practice dummy to fulfill your deepest fantasies of dismembering your enemies limb by limb on horseback. Might you have the skill required to dismount your challengers, you may just win The Goblin King's favor and the love of his subjects.

Mounted on horseback, players are sent galloping towards each-other. Each arm is controlled individually, and knights must be cautious to balance the placement of their lance and shield. When players collide, scores are tallied based on limb dismemberment and placement accuracy.

Rogue-Like Synergies

No matter what, players will be met with a challenge. Loser is given a choice between 3 modifiers. Choose to pimp out your ride or debuff your opponent. Should you send them flying with a rocket joust or buy them a dizzy lager potion? Even the best players will be on their toes.

Online Multiplayer

Create a private room for you and your close buddy, or join a random room so you can yell at a stranger as you insert a lance into their throbbing heart. Not enough for you? Of course not. Engage in tournament mode and compete against several players to be the very best blood-thirsty knight.

Achievements

You think you're good enough? Jousting Around doesn't. Not at least until you unlock all of the achievements. You will be allowed through the gates of Joust heaven only once you have dismembered enough heads and created the greatest synergies. Your plight will be amazing.

store_data.about_the_game:
Trade it, mine it, craft it, or shoot past it: how you survive the galaxy is up to you. Absolute Infinity is a small handcrafted 2D space simulator with living economies to work, pirates to fight, and ships to build.

Fly your own ships

Pilot a range of vessels, starting in a scrappy shuttle and work your way up to powerful capital ships. Purchase or craft upgrades for your ships, and outfit them to suit your style of play.

Craft and trade

Systems have markets that shift with supply, demand, and what you do to them. Haul goods from star to star and turn a profit by buying low and selling high. Or, mine and source ingredients yourself to craft over 50 unique items and sell them for a bigger profit.

Ship-to-ship combat

Hunt pirates, defend your cargo, and fight through anyone between you and the truth. Every projectile is simulated, and each hit carries weight. Slug it out in close quarters combat, or build a missile boat and blow your enemies out of the sky from a distance. The choice is yours.

Mod Support

Absolute Infinity's custom engine was built from the ground up with extensibility in mind, and comes with the same tools used to create it. You can extend the game by adding new ships, quests, items, and more.

store_data.about_the_game:
PLEIADES ZERO

Somewhere in the Pleiades cluster, a traveler named Beiling sets out across seven stars, each ruled by one of the Seven Sisters. To reach the seventh and final star is to reach the truth of the universe itself — a truth that will unmake everything Beiling believes about their own reality.

Pleiades Zero is a 2D maze-puzzle platformer built around movement, timing, and momentum. Every surface is a foothold: floors, walls, and ceilings all reset your jump, turning each chamber into a three-dimensional puzzle you solve with your feet. Armed with a laser whip to strike and a laser shield to survive, you'll fight, climb, and think your way toward the light of the seventh sister.

Features

  • Surface-jump traversal — bounce off any surface you touch, floors, walls, and ceilings alike, to thread mazes no ordinary jump could reach

  • Laser whip & laser shield — a two-button combat rhythm of attack and defense

  • Maze-puzzle platforming — navigation, timing, and spatial puzzles woven into every level

  • Seven stars, seven sisters — a journey through the Pleiades toward a truth that rewrites reality

  • A striking retro look — chunky pixel art beneath vast, minimalist alien skies

Seven sisters stand between Beiling and the truth. How far will you climb to see it?

Controls

  • A / D — Move left / right

  • W — Jump (touch any surface to reset your jump — yes, ceilings too)

  • Left Mouse — Laser whip

  • Right Mouse — Laser shield

  • Esc — Pause

store_data.about_the_game:
Cross the line. Learn what a life is worth.

In the megacity of Neo-Babylon, the law has one final clause: the moment a person's hidden wealth crosses one trillion dollars, they forfeit their right to live. You are K — the executioner who enforces that line.

But the numbers have started to lie. As you carry out one execution after another, a single question tightens around you: who decides the value of a human life — and what happens when the system itself is the criminal?

A story that branches on every choice

Your decisions reshape the plot, the people at your side, and the ending you reach. Five distinct endings. Two full routes. Nothing you do is forgotten — a choice in the first hour can change who lives in the last.

Cyberpunk noir, told with intent

Hand-drawn art, a rain-soaked dystopia, and a terse, hard-boiled script. Investigate crime scenes, read between the lines, and assemble the truth from what people refuse to say.

More than just reading

Hack terminals, route signals, and crack security in tactile minigames woven into the story — not busywork, but the moments K's hands do the work his conscience can't.

One hidden ending

Reach the TRUE END and a bonus story opens — one you won't see coming.

How much is a human life worth? Cross the line and find out.

Languages: English, 日本語 (full text). The game auto-selects your system language; switch anytime from the title screen.

content_descriptors.notes:
THE 13th Digit is a story-driven visual novel about state-sanctioned execution. The player character, K, is an executioner who carries out death sentences on people whose hidden wealth exceeds one trillion dollars.

The game depicts violence and death: characters are shot and killed on screen, including scenes of execution. Violence is shown in a stylized, hand-drawn art style — there is no dismemberment, torture, or graphic gore. It also deals with mature themes such as capital punishment, the value of a human life, institutional corruption, and moral responsibility for killing. There is one passing textual reference to a character discarding a cigarette.

The game does not contain sexual content or nudity, sexual assault or non-consensual sex, BDSM, drug abuse, self-harm, or suicide.

store_data.about_the_game:
COUNTER CLERK CONTRACT. The pawnshop.

The clerk answers for what they buy. Three bad calls in one day and you are dismissed on the spot. Wages settle each night: a base, plus a little more for every good buy. The clerk's own pawn, ticket No. 0031, keeps running. Thirty a night, owed apart from your wage. Miss three payments and the house keeps what you pledged.

Sign here x                                         

Are you the Expert?

You're the new hire behind the counter of a neighborhood pawnshop, the kind that buys what people can't afford to keep. You took the job because you needed it, and because something of yours is already back there in the boss's case, the interest ticking up every night. Everyone who walks up has a story about why their stuff is worth more than it is. Some are telling the truth. Most aren't.

Your job is to catch the lie. Among the regulars bringing in rings, watches, and old guitars are undercover cops, wanted faces off the morning bulletin, and people asking a favor you'll regret. Each item lands on your counter and the call is yours: buy it, refuse it, or pick up the phone and report it. The boss teaches you one new thing to check every day and it never leaves you. Get it right and you inch back toward buying your own pledge out of that case. Get it wrong and it's gone.

All brands, serials and signatures in the game are fictional.

In the very far future, the sun is in its final stage of life. Earth has become a desert. Water is severally depleted and greenery is extremely rare. Despite this, humanity still persist. You will have to be tactical take your enemies down. You will need to master combat, as the enemies will get more dangerous as you progress. Good news is you have a map to help explore and permanent upgrades to improve your combat capabilities.

Good Luck!

store_data.about_the_game:
⚠ Development Notice

All screenshots and videos were captured from a pre-alpha build. The game is under active development, and all visuals, gameplay, animations, UI, and content are subject to change.

Half a millennium has passed since the fall of the Cult of the Free Mind, yet its whispers echo from the shadows once more. What was long believed to be nothing more than legend is beginning to take physical form.

Farreach has fallen into bloodshed, paranoia, and tyranny.. You are Edfred, the bastard son of a local lord, who must earn the right to restore his family's legacy and prepare its people for what is relentlessly drawing near.

Restore a Fading Legacy

Your journey begins not with power, but with earning the right to wield it. Win the trust of your people, unite allies under your banner, and transform a crumbling settlement into a stronghold capable of withstanding the coming chaos.

Manage your settlement, balance the needs of its people, the demands of the nobility, and your limited resources. Recruit and develop your own guard companies to reclaim the surrounding lands and gradually restore your family's legacy.

Deep Turn-Based Tactical Combat

No class restrictions—only the freedom to experiment. Combine skills, spells, and magical items to create a playstyle that is uniquely your own.

Take advantage of elevation, terrain, and interactive battlefields. Manage your party's morale and shatter your enemies' morale, and prepare carefully before every encounter.

The World Moves On

Events will not wait for your decisions. Events move forward relentlessly, and your choices determine not whether they happen, but what their consequences will be.

In a world where the line between good and evil has long since faded, every choice comes at a cost. Allies may become enemies, while former enemies may become unexpected allies.

Beyond Good and Evil

Everyone you meet carries secrets from the past, old wounds, and hidden motives. The past has left scars on everyone, and personal convictions often outweigh any sense of right or wrong.

Half a millennium has passed since the fall of the Cult of the Free Mind, yet its whispers echo from the shadows once more. What was long believed to be nothing more than legend is beginning to take physical form.

Farreach has fallen into bloodshed, paranoia, and tyranny.. You are Edfred, the bastard son of a local lord, who must earn the right to restore his family's legacy and prepare its people for what is relentlessly drawing near.

Restore a Fading Legacy

Your journey begins not with power, but with earning the right to wield it. Win the trust of your people, unite allies under your banner, and transform a crumbling settlement into a stronghold capable of withstanding the coming chaos.

Manage your settlement, balance the needs of its people, the demands of the nobility, and your limited resources. Recruit and develop your own guard companies to reclaim the surrounding lands and gradually restore your family's legacy.

Deep Turn-Based Tactical Combat

No class restrictions—only the freedom to experiment. Combine skills, spells, and magical items to create a playstyle that is uniquely your own.

Take advantage of elevation, terrain, and interactive battlefields. Manage your party's morale and shatter your enemies' morale, and prepare carefully before every encounter.

The World Moves On

Events will not wait for your decisions. Events move forward relentlessly, and your choices determine not whether they happen, but what their consequences will be.

In a world where the line between good and evil has long since faded, every choice comes at a cost. Allies may become enemies, while former enemies may become unexpected allies.

Beyond Good and Evil

Everyone you meet carries secrets from the past, old wounds, and hidden motives. The past has left scars on everyone, and personal convictions often outweigh any sense of right or wrong.

In this world, it is never easy to tell who is a friend—and who is the real monster.

 

Will you preserve order in a world falling apart, or let the Blight consume your very soul?

store_data.about_the_game:
Star Claw is a cosmic-gothic claw-machine roguelite where every grab is a trick shot. Time the swing, fling a cat's spectral paw through haunted prize rooms, and bank off bumpers to turn impossible angles into a collection that follows you home.

FLING. BANK. GRAB.

Watch the swing, launch at the right moment, and bank off bumpers to reach prizes a straight shot can't. Chain clean grabs, manage the clock, and push riskier angles for bigger payouts.

READ EACH ROOM

Prize layouts, moving hazards, and room rules keep changing. Read the board, adjust your angle, and decide when the dangerous shot is worth it.

THREAD YOUR PAWCRAFT

Build a four-command loadout from the Pawcraft you collect. Call a second paw, nudge the board, phase through a target, or clear nearby hazards.

CHOOSE THE NEXT THREAD

When the Starpath forks, stay the course or take a Mystery Path for a harder branch and a richer payout.

BUILD A STRANGE COLLECTION

Open Kitty Capsules and themed decor collections in Capsule Hall. Discover new cats, room pieces, and rare cursor styles, then choose what follows you home.

CHOOSE A CAT. CHANGE THE RUN.

Choose a collected cat before each run. Every one brings a gameplay perk, from extra Swats to more valuable prizes.

MAKE MY ROOM YOURS

Return to Star City between runs, arrange unlocked decor in My Room, choose a legendary backdrop, and watch your cats move in.

PLAY SOLO OR CO-OP

Chase the next prize solo or team up in co-op. Your Pawcraft, route, and chosen cat shape every run; every find gives you something new to bring home.

4984690.name: Tanach: A Journey Through the Hebrew Bible

store_data.about_the_game:
The whole Hebrew Bible, beautifully lit

It's a big, sprawling library — Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim, 39 books across 929 chapters — and this is an unhurried, lamp-lit way to come to know it. Every question is drawn straight from the text. Answer one, and the verse it came from opens up in front of you: the original Hebrew beside the plain JPS English. You're never just guessing at trivia — you're reading the source, a few lines at a time.

Every answer leaves you with something

Right or wrong, the game shows you where the words come from and what they mean, in a short, plain note. Miss one and you'll remember it next time. Get it, and you'll have earned it — not memorized a fact, but met a verse.

Read it, hear it, sit with it

A full reader lives beside the quiz. Open any chapter, let it be read aloud, tap a word you don't recognize to see what it means, and jump from a question straight to the verse it quotes. Study whichever way suits you:

• By book or parasha — walk from Genesis to Chronicles at your own pace.

• The Daily Challenge — ten questions from across the Tanach to start the day.

• By theme — follow a thread through the whole thing: Creation, Covenant, Kings, Prophecy, Wisdom, Exile, the women of the Tanach.

• At your level — three tiers, from first steps to the deep cuts.

Made to return to

See how you're doing, book by book, and find the spots worth another look. Keep a daily streak going. Collect illuminated cards and quietly earn 63 achievements named for the tradition itself. It reads your controller on the couch and runs on the Steam Deck on the train — with colorblind-friendly feedback, a reduced-motion option, and full keyboard play. It's built to be picked up again tomorrow.

A word about the text

The scripture is the public-domain JPS 1917 translation, kept word for word, so a verse reads the same in a question as it does in the reader. It's been carefully checked for accuracy and tone against that text. Think of it as a study companion made with care — a doorway into the Tanach, not a religious authority.

SHADOW RUNNER

The signal breaks. No commands left — only the hum of something older. Your blade answers first.

SHADOW RUNNER is a fast, unforgiving action-roguelike about one runner, one katana, and a descent that doesn't let you back out.

Cut with intent

A combat system built for expression, not button-mashing:

  • Three-phase combos that flow into aerial dives and ground plunges

  • Dive-cancel and dash to rewrite your spacing mid-fight

  • Sub-weapons — drone, grenade, knife, disc, tether, skull — swap to fit the run

  • Hit-pause and slow-mo that make every clean kill land

No two runs the same

  • Curses — opt into penalties for stacked rewards; reshape the rules of a run

  • Loot & gear with affixes, set bonuses, and game-changing uniques

  • Upgrades & shrines drafted between waves

  • Challenge arenas behind sealed doors for the greedy

Descend

  • 12 chapters from the Corridor to the First Dark

  • 23 enemy types and 4 bosses — the Voidlord, the Sovereign, the Forge, the Eye

  • Endless mode — how deep can you go?

Style

Neon-soaked pixel carnage, hand-tuned game feel, and a fully procedural audio engine. One blade. No retreat.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dig deeper. Cause the disaster. Escape before the planet buries you.

CoreVore is a single-player mining roguelite built around destructible voxel worlds and systemic physics. Land on procedural planets, scan the depths, extract valuable ore, and send your haul into orbit.

But remember: the planet itself is your enemy, and every disaster is brought closer by your own decisions.

Remove a support and the ceiling may collapse. Breach an underground lake and your mine begins to flood. Cut too close to lava and you might seal your only route home. Water flows, ice melts, lava hardens, loose rock gives way, and a wounded planet begins to shake beneath your feet.

These systems collide to turn every expedition into a new story.

Destroy—and live with the consequences

Every tunnel changes the planet. Damage to the rock persists for the entire expedition, structural supports matter, and aggressive mining destabilizes the world faster.

The deeper you descend, the richer the deposits become—and the more dangerous the journey back.

Choose the right tool

Use the Laser to extract ore with precision. The Volume Cutter carves tunnels quickly but leaves no valuable drops behind. Scan for deposits through solid rock. Freeze water, harden lava, and melt ice with Thermal mode. Blast through sealed passages with explosive Charges—but risk destroying the ore inside.

Every tool solves one problem while creating another.

Deploy temporary machinery

Set up autonomous Drill Rigs, Stabilizers, Drainers, Hardeners, and Light Beacons. Each machine controls a limited working area, but none of them makes the planet safe.

An undermined floor, a cave-in, or a lava breach can destroy your investment. There are no permanent bases here: recover your equipment or leave it behind.

Secure your haul—or risk one more run

Store your cargo in the escape pod and launch protected batches into orbit during the expedition. Everything you send is permanently secured. Everything you keep with you can still be lost.

Evacuate now—or make one more push for a richer vein. That is the defining choice of every expedition.

Grow stronger—or buy your freedom

Between expeditions, choose one of three routes, sell resources, complete contracts, purchase blueprints, and craft permanent modules from the materials you bring home.

New abilities open access to more dangerous planets. But every credit spent on becoming stronger delays your ultimate goal: paying off the debt on your ship.

store_data.about_the_game:
The bank wants a million dollars. You have a computer and a lot of free time.

You boot up EggOS, a cheerful little egg-themed operating system, to find one email waiting: the bank is foreclosing on your house unless you can pay back $1,000,000. So you do the only sensible thing — you open a code editor and start making games.

Ship your first game

Hammer the keyboard in the Code Editor to churn out Lines of Code, compile them into Features in the Dev Shop, and reinvest in upgrades and automation — a Coding AI that writes for you, an Auto-Compiler that never sleeps — until you can finally build and ship your game.

Market it, launch it, sell it

  • Video Studio — a physics dart-throwing range. Hit the growing bullseye for Wishlists.

  • Launch — spend your Wishlists to release your game to the world.

  • Sales Floor — a three-reel slot machine that turns hype into cash, until the bank is finally PAID.

A desktop full of distractions

EggOS isn't a menu — it's a tiny operating system you play inside. Draggable windows, notifications, a screensaver, golden eggs that trigger score Frenzies, and bugs that crawl across your desktop to swat. Plus bite-sized side games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, and a Slide Puzzle.

Open a New Studio (Prestige)

Start fresh to earn Prestige points and spend them on a sprawling skill tree of permanent multipliers, head-starts, and game-changing perks. Every studio is faster than the last — and idle progress means the work keeps going while you're away.

Features at a glance

  • A playable fake-desktop OS — windows, taskbar, notifications, critters and all

  • A layered incremental loop: code → market → launch → sell → prestige

  • Real mini-games, not just number-go-up: dart physics and a rigged slot machine

  • Bonus side games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, Slide Puzzle

  • A deep Prestige skill tree with stacking multipliers

  • Idle & offline earnings

  • One clear goal: pay off the bank before it takes your house

Make games. Beat the bank. Then do it all again, faster.

store_data.about_the_game:
The lights are off. The van is waiting. Who stole it?

Who Stole It! is a cartoon cops-and-robbers party game. Thieves sneak through a museum at night, grabbing paintings, gems and gold and smuggling them out to the getaway van. The police hunt them down — and in this game nobody dies. You get ARRESTED, locked in a cell, and your friends have to break you out.

Two ways to play every night

  • Thief — watch the patrol, wait for your moment, grab, run, deliver. Then get greedy for one more painting… and get caught red-handed.

  • Police — patrol the halls, watch the CCTV monitors, cut the power to set traps, and march every last thief into a prison cell.

Meet the cast

10 characters, each with their own tricks:

  • The Clown drops fake copies of himself — arrest the wrong one and the fine comes out of YOUR pocket.

  • The Ghost Kid kills the lights and summons a crowd of ghosts to guard him.

  • The Timekeeper picks the prison lock and frees the whole cell.

  • The Wanderer has no powers at all. Pure skill, pure nerve.

…plus sneaky scouts, dapper counts and hard-nosed officers to match your playstyle.

Tools of the trade

Smoke bombs. Decoys. Power cuts that plunge the museum into darkness. Fires that cost the city money if the police ignore them. Security cameras, vents, and one very tempting getaway van.

Never wait in an empty lobby

Play solo against AI thieves, or host for friends — bots fill every empty seat in the crew and hand their spot to real players who join. Two players are enough to start the night.

Features

  • Asymmetric multiplayer — thieves vs police.

  • 10 playable characters with unique abilities.

  • Arrests instead of deaths: jail time, sentences, prison breaks.

  • Optional chaos rule: caught thieves join the police.

  • Single player vs bots, online with bot backfill.

  • In-game voice chat, text chat, mute and kick.

  • Menus in 16 languages.

store_data.about_the_game:
Word Cubes is a challenging 3D word game that reimagines the classic tile-placing experience on a three-dimensional grid. Place letter tiles across a vibrant cubic board, form intersecting words in multiple directions, and outscore your CPU opponent in this addictive puzzle game.

**Key Features:**

• **3D Gameplay** — Place tiles across three axes on a striking cubic board. Think in three dimensions as you build words along the X, Y, and Z axes, creating unexpected intersections and strategic depth you won't find in traditional games.

• **Strategic Tile Placement** — With premium bonus squares including Double Word, Triple Word, Double Letter, and Triple Letter multipliers scattered across the cube's faces, every placement is a calculated decision. Maximize your score by controlling the most valuable spaces.

• **Standard Letter Distribution** — Play with familiar letter values and frequencies matching classic English word games. Rare letters like Q, Z, and J carry higher point values, while common letters like E and A offer safer, lower-risk plays.

• **Smart AI Opponents** — Challenge yourself against adjustable difficulty AI. The computer opponent analyzes the board, forms high-scoring words, and plays strategically to test your skills.

• **Tactical Swaps** — Running low on options? Swap tiles from your rack back into the bag for a fresh draw. Manage your resources wisely — passing costs you a turn but can set up bigger plays later.

• **Clean 3D Visuals** — Rotate, zoom, and inspect the board from any angle. The polished 3D presentation makes it easy to see connections across all three axes and plan your next move.

• **Instant Word Validation** — Real-time feedback shows whether your formed words are valid as you place tiles. The pending score display keeps you informed of your potential points before committing to a play.

**How to Play:**

Select a tile from your rack of seven, then move the cursor across the 3D grid to position it. Lock your placement direction and commit your word. Form words along any axis — horizontal, vertical, or depth — and create cross-words for bonus points. Your first move must cover the center of the cube; subsequent plays must connect to existing tiles.

The game ends when all tiles are exhausted, or players have passed too many times. The player with the highest score wins.

store_data.about_the_game:
POST-SCARCITY SCIENCE-FICTION GRAND STRATEGY


The Helios Accord is a post-scarcity science-fiction grand strategy game about governing a civilization shared by humans and Citizen Minds. Power is abundant. Legitimacy must be earned.

As impossible signals return from beyond known space, every observation reveals more—and gives something unknown another chance to learn how the Accord communicates, decides, and defends itself.

GOVERN A POST-SCARCITY CIVILIZATION


Set doctrine, allocate attention, spend public mandate, negotiate with other civilizations, and authorize expeditions across a frontier where material abundance has not made difficult choices disappear.

MAKE POLICY IN PUBLIC


Read petitions, inspect evidence, hear dissent, and commit the Accord to promises that constrain future action. Every intervention changes trust, rights, and the institutions that made the decision possible.

SHARE POWER WITH CITIZEN MINDS


Citizen Minds are superintelligent created people with memory, relationships, political standing, and the right to refuse. They advise the public, carry expeditions, coordinate habitats, preserve archives, and decide whether to accept dangerous work.

NEGOTIATE ACROSS CIVILIZATIONS


Rescue, quarantine, dialogue, concealment, and resistance expose different parts of the Accord. A successful intervention may preserve lives while teaching something unknown how the civilization responds.

INVESTIGATE THE IMPOSSIBLE


Trace signals that arrive out of sequence. Audit records that are individually valid and mutually incompatible. Follow routes that leave the known map and return carrying evidence that no one knows how to interpret safely.

LIVE WITH THE RECORD


Forecasts, objections, consequences, harm, and repair remain attached to the decisions that produced them. The public record remembers what the Accord promised—even when the archive no longer agrees on what happened.

SOMETHING HAS LEARNED THE WAY HOME.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build a ridiculous space empire—one bot, rocket, and planet at a time

Idle empire parody meets cozy-chaotic progression. Hire Optimax bots, launch rockets, and terraform whole solar systems while your multi-world campaign spirals into increasingly absurd scale. If you love the loop of Cookie Clicker-style growth, clever automation, and “wait… that combo just broke everything” moments, this is your next obsession.

What you do

You run an empire that starts small and refuses to stay that way. Recruit Optimax bots to automate production and expansion. Fire rockets to push farther into space. Terraform planets and, eventually, entire solar systems. Every upgrade, hire, and launch feeds the same addictive cycle: do a little, unlock a lot, then watch the numbers—and the worlds—explode.

This is an idle empire-building game first: strong passive progress, active planning when you want it, and constant reasons to come back for “just one more” synergy.

Grow across worlds, not just meters

Progress isn’t a single endless bar. You’re on a multi-world campaign where each stage opens new systems, new pressure, and new ways to specialize. Expand your reach, retool your bot workforce, and turn raw industrial chaos into a polished (or gloriously unhinged) interplanetary machine.

Living 3D planets make that growth feel tangible. You’re not only reading stats—you’re watching worlds change as your empire digs in, industrializes, and remakes them.

Hidden synergies and a secret machine-world path

The obvious upgrades are only half the fun. Buried in the systems are hidden synergies: odd pairings, delayed payoffs, and “I didn’t know that stacked” discoveries that rewire your whole strategy.

And then there’s the secret machine-world path—a deeper route for players who dig, experiment, and refuse to play the safe line. Chase efficiency, chase weirdness, or chase both. The empire doesn’t care how tasteful your choices are, only that they scale.

Cozy chaos, serious scale

The tone is parody with a soft landing: approachable, playful, and a little unhinged, without needing a spreadsheet personality to enjoy it. Drop in for a few active decisions, then let Optimax bots and automation carry the grind. Come back later to a bigger map, better rockets, more terraforming power, and new combos begging to be abused.

Expect:

[*] Idle / incremental empire progression with active moments that matter

[*] Optimax bots to hire, assign, and automate your rise

[*] Rockets, expansion, and full solar-system terraforming goals

[*] A multi-world campaign structure instead of a single flat loop

[*] Hidden synergies that reward curiosity and experimentation

[*] A secret machine-world path for deeper, stranger progression

[*] Living 3D planets that visualize your conquest and conversion

[*] Cozy-chaotic Cookie Clicker energy with space-empire absurdity

Who it’s for

Perfect if you want an idle game with personality, a parody empire fantasy that doesn’t take itself too seriously, and enough systems under the hood to keep theory-crafters and chill clickers both happy. Build bots. Launch rockets. Terraform everything in sight. Then find the combo that makes the solar system politely give up.

Your empire is waiting. Optimax already printed the onboarding pamphlet. It may be slightly on fire.

store_data.about_the_game:
Somewhere out there is an old brick-breaker cabinet that keeps more than high scores.

FIRST LIGHT is a story-rich arcade brick-breaker: classic paddle-and-ball play, rebuilt around a family's whole century — one memory per level, told in four voices, sealed against the Fog that takes unwitnessed things. Every wall you break is the Fog's work undone.

THE TELLING

  • 132 memories across four acts — a grandmother's river town, a father's long yard, a boy's 1986 arcade summer… and the fourth act the machine was built to keep
  • Fully voiced by four narrators, one memory before every level — listen, or skip straight to the bricks
  • Four paintings hidden behind the four bosses, revealed brick by brick
  • An original 36-song soundtrack, scored so each memory plays the song that agrees with it

THE GAME

  • Honest arcade brick-breaking — reflexes, angles, and nerve, easy to start and hard to put down
  • A capsule economy that pays for risk: stack multipliers, bank speed, grow the light cannon — or catch the black pill on purpose
  • Four difficulties, from a gentle telling to one-life INSANE
  • Boss walls where the Fog itself fights back — play calm; walls come down for patient hands
  • 33 achievements, three save campaigns, a high-score board with one name already on it: M-E-G

6–8 HOURS OF STORY — AND THE LIGHT AFTER

Beat it for the telling. Come back for AFTERGLOW — just the music, no dying, endless — the achievement hunt, and the board MEG left you to beat.

Football Fictional World Simulator is a game about watching football history happen—and deciding when to give it a small push.

You are not a manager. You do not select lineups, design tactics, run training sessions or control matches. The clubs and national teams make those decisions for themselves. Your direct involvement is focused entirely on the transfer market.

Clubs identify players, negotiate deals and bring transfer proposals to you. You decide whether each move should be approved or rejected. A single decision might change a player’s career, rescue a struggling club or alter the balance of an entire league.

There are two ways to play:

  • Intervene in the transfer market and influence the football world

  • Leave every decision to the clubs and play as a completely hands-off observer

You can move freely between these styles. Approve a few transfers that interest you, then step back and watch their consequences unfold over the next five, ten or fifty years.

The game simulates a large fictional football world:

  • 63 countries and 94 leagues across five continents

  • Major competitions and smaller, less familiar leagues

  • Promotion and relegation

  • Domestic leagues and cup competitions

  • Continental club tournaments

  • Senior, U-23 and U-20 national teams

  • World Cup qualifying and continental championships

  • Player development, transfers, retirement and new generations

  • Seasonal awards, Best XIs and historical records

A full year can be simulated in around ten minutes, depending on your computer. This makes it possible to move far beyond the length of a normal football career. You can follow a promising teenager until retirement, watch a small club gradually become a continental power, or simulate 100 years and explore a football world that no longer resembles the one you started with.

Matches are handled by a text-based match engine. Results are not simply selected from a random score table. Player attributes, positions, formations, team strength, attacking moves, shots, saves, substitutions and the changing state of the match all affect what happens.

After each season, you can explore far more than goals and assists:

  • Appearances, starts and substitute appearances

  • Average match ratings

  • Shots and shots on target

  • Passing, defensive and goalkeeper statistics

  • Player careers and transfer histories

  • Club and competition records

  • Seasonal, regional and world Best XIs

The transfer system is deliberately limited. You cannot freely sign every talented young player or rebuild a club in a single transfer window. Clubs choose their own targets, players sometimes move to unexpected destinations, and the ideal proposal may never arrive. Your role feels less like personally constructing a squad and more like giving the final signature to decisions made by the football world around you.

Club football includes domestic competitions and continental tournaments such as the Champions League, Europa League, AFC Champions League and Copa Libertadores. International football includes World Cup qualification, continental championships, the Olympic tournament and U-20 competitions.

Over time, the results begin to feel like a history of their own. A striker from a minor league may become the greatest international scorer of his generation. A former powerhouse may spend decades outside the top division. A small country may produce an exceptional generation and reach a World Cup final.

You can influence this world through transfers, or simply let it run. Either way, the game is about finding the stories that only appear when football is given enough time.

store_data.about_the_game:
Goodly Trials is a turn-based game of strategy and resource. Hire a peculiar company of knights, sell-swords, merchants, and magic-men, arm them as you please, arrange the line, and survive your journey home.

Some will help you for coin.

Some, because the road was worse alone.

Journey alone.. 

In the single-player journey, draft a leader and a defining trait, then follow the hard rhythm of the road:

Shop → Place → Equip → Battle → Plan → Shop..

You can endure three losses in combat, but need to survive for twelve weeks. Harder trials bring crueler foes. Deeds earned along the way open the door to new recruits, gear, traits, boss battles, and new factions.. the persistent Bone Host, and the treasure-obsessed Below Born.

Or with agreeable company

In multiplayer, 2 to 8 players share a tournament and regrettably, the markets as well.

Bid against other players for the same recruits and gear, arrange your company in peace, and meet each rival in a turn-based league. Bring friends, fill empty seats with AI armies, wager on featured matches, and remember who it was that increased the price paid for your squire.

Climb the ranked ladder

In ranked, your armies face companies built by ruthless AI, and eventually other players from the closed beta (and Early Access). A rating follows every result, matching you with opponents who have proved roughly as dangerous as you. Win and climb to earn rare rewards.

Goodly Trials Gameplay

  • Goodly Trials is turn-based: The road will wait while you think.

  • No two bargains are quite alike: Units and gear bear innate attributes and rolled traits that change what they are good for. An otherwise ordinary hire may become the strange hinge upon which the whole company turns. The market does not ask whether a recruit is good. It asks whether you can imagine a good use for this one.

  • Auto-battler: The field and your company grow throughout the journey. Small skirmishes become full formations, where range, formation, flanking, adjacency, and the shape of the opposing line all matter. The battle itself demands no hurried commands. Once committed, your company proves the strength of your tactics.

Developer's statement:

Thanks for taking a look at Goodly Trials. It has become exactly the game I hoped to make.

It is also the game I have wanted to play as I have gotten older, with less time for grinding, less aptitude for the APM demands of MOBAs, and no patience for pay-to-win designs.

Lastly, artistically it lives up to my values. Goodly Trials will always be small and precise enough that I, (or another) artist draw by hand, every image of every frame, from the mouse cursor to the bosses and their grand weapons. AI is changing everything in the world it seems, but it will have no impart on the design of Goodly Trials.

It is a little game with big ideas. I hope you enjoy it.

-Taylor

store_data.about_the_game:
A chess where you don't capture — you grind them down.

Damage Chess rebuilds chess around HP, Attack and Defense. Pieces no longer fall in one hit. You chip away their HP, and only defeat them when it reaches zero. Damage is randomized, and an attacked piece may strike back. Every square becomes a gamble.

Three actions a turn — dense, deliberate play.

Instead of one move, you take three actions per turn. Advance, corner them, and strike. There is no checkmate — the first player to burn the enemy King's HP to zero wins.

Chess's special moves, weaponized.

Castle to shelter your King, stab with en passant, and choose Q/R/B/N on promotion (current HP carries over). The classic rules mesh with HP combat into something new.

Tune the luck yourself.

Damage variance, counter success rate, actions per turn, special-rule toggles — the rules are yours. You can even edit each piece's HP, Attack and Defense individually.

A CPU with real bite — and friends around the world.

Four CPU tiers: Weak / Normal / Strong / Expert. Play friends online (invite / room code, reconnection support).

FEATURES

🎯 A fresh chess battle driven by HP / Attack / Defense — defeat a piece to advance onto its square
♟ Full castling, en passant, double-step and Q/R/B/N promotion
🎲 Randomized damage and counterattacks create constant tension (adjustable variance and rate)
⚡ Three actions per turn for deep tactical sequencing
🤖 Four CPU difficulty tiers
🌐 Online play with friends (invite / room code, reconnection support)
🛠 Fully customizable rules and piece stats
🎌 Japanese and English

The second title from Ichigeki Games, creators of Damage Shogi.
