store_data.about_the_game:
Join the Airborne, and join the fight against Communism!

(Side effects include caffeine addiction and pointing at things with a knife-hand.)

So much coffee. So much firepower. So much love for Democracy.

You’re Giga Joe, a highly trained (and slightly unhinged) paratrooper dropped behind enemy lines to cause as much damage as humanly possible. Blast through waves of Soviets, decimate Communist bosses, and leave a trail of pixelated destruction in this pure arcade run-and-gun.

15 minutes of explosive campaign chaos, then Endless mode when you’re ready to test yourself. With a driving soundtrack by Bert Cole, crisp pixel art, and, um, "enthusiastic" voice acting.

Features

  • Set in the world of the ttrpg Mörk Borg hack, Victory's Grave

  • Classic top-down run-and-gun gameplay inspired by the arcade greats

  • Tight campaign (~15 minutes) plus endless survival mode with scaling difficulty

  • Wide variety of enemies, challenging bosses, and explosive encounters

  • Powerful weapons and satisfying combat loop

  • Original score by Bert Cole

  • "Enthusiastic" voice acting

  • Fully offline – jump in and play anytime

  • PWYW – pay what you want

Controls & Tech Specs

  • Keyboard + mouse (WASD movement, mouse aim & shoot)

  • Gamepad fully supported

  • Windows – play offline with no restrictions

  • Dev team led by Lewis Manalo, military veteran and writer for Ghost Recon: Wildlands and more

Lock and load, Airborne. It's time to kick some Commie butt!

store_data.about_the_game:
The shift has begun. Time to save the city!

Bad Dead Shift is a dynamic side-scrolling pixel shooter that blends intense action, level exploration, and chaotic zombie combat. The undead don’t just shuffle forward - they grab weapons, shoot back, surround you, and keep you moving constantly!

Knock a shotgun out of an infected’s hands with a powerful bat swing. Pick it up and clear the room. Out of ammo? No problem - hurl the empty gun straight into the next zombie’s face. Every second of combat is a choice between risk and mayhem.

Levels are built from rooms and corridors, where every door hides the unknown. A new room might reward you with rescued survivors... or a deadly ambush. And in dark basements, you'd better not linger - you never know who's waiting in the shadows.

Save survivors, unlock new hats, and change your playstyle. Cop, firefighter, cowboy, soldier, or even a magician - each hat changes the rules of battle and lets you approach levels in fresh new ways.

Want a real challenge? Jump into Arcade Mode and try to survive an endless night in a city that's already almost dead.

  • Armed zombies - The infected don't just charge ahead. They grab guns, shoot back, and turn every room into an unpredictable firefight.

  • Hit, knock, improvise - Charge your baseball bat, knock weapons out of enemies' hands, and use everything around you - even throw empty guns as a last resort to stay alive.

  • 30 dangerous levels - Open doors blindly, explore rooms, and descend into dark basements where a deadly ambush could be hiding behind every shadow.

  • Huge arsenal of crazy weapons - From the classic bat to miniguns, flamethrowers, and laser guns, each weapon changes the rhythm of combat.

  • Game-changing hats - Save survivors, unlock new looks, and pick bonuses that completely change your approach to clearing levels.

store_data.about_the_game:
Imperionis is a single-player tactical RPG in which you take the role of a Roman commander and lead a century through a military campaign in Gaul. The campaign lasts 150 in-game days, with three actions available each day. You decide whether to spend them on training, treatment, rest, camp development, or advancing along the route.

During the campaign, text-based events present several possible actions. Their outcomes depend on the commander’s attributes, the condition of the century, equipment, and a D20 roll. Your decisions affect health, morale, supplies, troop strength, and the conditions of future battles.

The commander and the century develop separately. The commander improves personal attributes and combat skills while acquiring weapons, armor, and travel equipment. The army unlocks new doctrines, orders, characters, and units, including legionaries, auxiliary infantry, ranged troops, cavalry, standard-bearers, scorpions, and onagers. Each troop branch earns its own veterancy and performs a distinct role within the battle group.

Key features:

  • turn-based battles on a hex grid featuring multiple controllable units, different attack types, and movement ranges, playable manually or through autobattle;

  • century development with new characters, troop types, orders, and tactical options to unlock;

  • separate veterancy progression for infantry, ranged troops, cavalry, standard-bearers, and siege crews;

  • varied objectives, including eliminating the enemy, holding a position, breaking through a formation, protecting a unit, and defeating an enemy commander;

  • personal duels against enemies who break through to the commander, using his attributes, combat skills, and equipment;

  • camp development and management of supplies, medicine, morale, and troop strength;

  • campaign-ending death or loss of the century, followed by a legacy system for future campaigns.

Check results, chosen development paths, unlocked units, and battle losses affect how the campaign unfolds. Both the century’s tactical battles and the commander’s personal duels can be played manually or resolved through autobattle.

store_data.about_the_game:
One more run. That's the whole game.

Fight waves of medieval hordes in first person, with up to three friends. Between waves you spend your gold at the shop. After every boss you pick one of three relics that bend the rules. Wipe, unlock something permanent, queue it up again.

The loop

Enemies camp around the map and you choose which fight to pick. Dawdle too long and the pressure clock wakes everything at once, faster and angrier than it was a minute ago. Clear the wave, crack the chest, sort your loot, vote to push on. A boss every five waves. Kill three of them and you've won. Then Endless mode asks if you really meant it.

Gear worth fighting over (except you can't)

Every drop is yours alone. Your loot is invisible to your friends, so nobody races you to the corpse and the group stays a group. Rarity decides how many affixes an item rolls and how spicy the rolls get, and the ceiling climbs every wave, so wave 12 loot makes wave 2 loot look like a costume. Want to trade anyway? Drop it on the ground like a gentleman.

Vendors with questionable ethics

After each boss a stall opens: the Blacksmith rerolls your gear until it's what you wanted it to be, or the Alchemist sells elixirs and a Mystery Tonic that permanently changes a random stat with zero refunds. And sometimes, mid-run, a Gambler just wanders in from parts unknown. You can guess how his prices work.

Abilities, picked at the worst possible time

Leveling up heals you to full and hands you a pick-one-of-three ability choice the moment things calm down. Stack up to four actives, feed them all from the same stamina pool that runs your dodges and swings, and decide mid-horde whether you can afford to cast anything at all.

Co-op that respects your evening

1 to 4 players, friends-only invites, no matchmaking queue. It's free, so the hardest part of getting your group together is already solved. Downed friends can be picked back up. Clutch revives are the best thing in the game, and I will not be taking questions.

What's actually in it

A run you can win, an Endless mode for people who don't believe in endings, six enemy types plus elite variants, bosses, personal loot with real itemization, ability builds, and milestone unlocks between runs. It's small on purpose and free on purpose. Some of the jank is load-bearing. If it's not for you, the uninstall button costs the same as the install button did.

store_data.about_the_game:
El sonido de un sueño is a first-person Venezuelan folk horror game inspired by the legend of El Silbón.

After returning to the Venezuelan plains, Andrés finds himself trapped inside a nightmare shaped by memory, guilt and loss. What begins as a quiet visit to an old rural house soon becomes a night of fear, silence and pursuit.

In this experience, there is no combat. You must explore, listen, hide, solve small environmental puzzles and survive the presence that follows you through the darkness.

Features:

  • First-person survival horror without combat.

  • A story inspired by Venezuelan folklore and rural legends.

  • Exploration through houses, roads, dark interiors and forgotten places.

  • Sound-driven tension where the whistle becomes a warning.

  • Environmental puzzles connected to memory, family and guilt.

  • A short atmospheric horror experience focused on tension, vulnerability and storytelling.

When the whistle sounds far away, it is already too late.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOUR OWN FOOTBALL CLUB

The club develops through your decisions. Sign players, improve the squad, change the way the team plays, and push for promotion. Poor recruitment can hold the club back for years, while the right group of players can carry it far beyond expectations.

THE MATCHES

Matches can be viewed in a voxel-style 3D stadium or through a 2D match view. Watch the full 90 minutes and jump between highlights, or follow the action through several camera options.

Live commentary, player ratings, match statistics, lineups, and post-match reports show the full picture.

THE TEAM

Set formations, player roles, duties, mentality, and tactical style. Players can also be moved freely on the pitch when you want to build a custom shape.

Each player has more than 30 attributes: potential, traits, form, fitness, chemistry, and more, all of which affect how they perform and how effective they are over time.

Assign specialist coaches and use experienced mentors to teach new traits.

THE CLUB

Scouts can be sent to different regions or instructed to search for specific positions. Their quality affects what kind of players they can find.

Negotiate fees, wages, contract length, and release clauses before deciding whether a deal is worth the cost.

Sponsors provide objectives during the season. Stadium upgrades, training facilities, ticket prices, wages, and operating costs all influence the club’s finances.

Use the medical center to manage injuries, player fitness, and morale throughout the season.

THE LEGACY

Season records include top scorers, average ratings, league awards, and player achievements. Footballers improve, age, decline, and eventually retire, forcing the club to keep changing.

4993800.name: Out Of Order - A Vending Machine Roguelike

store_data.about_the_game:
Out of Order is a cozy roguelike deckbuilder about running a vending machine. Your stockroom is your deck, every day is one round of restocking, selling, and drafting new products. An increasing weekly quota decides whether your contract survives.

A run is twelve weeks at one venue. Stock the machine well and profit; stock it poorly and customers walk away, perishables spoil, and the weekly quota check ends the contract.

Each day you restock your vending machine from your stockroom, serve the day's customers, and choose one of three new products to add to your deck. Chocolate pays more next to drinks, an energy drink provides a bonus for whoever's next in line, and a pizza slice pays a bonus if it empties the entire machine. Survive all twelve weekly quota checks to win the run.

What's in the game:

- 50 food and drink products

- 25 venues, from a laundromat to an international airport, each with its own crowd, commission cut, and quota curve

- 27 customers with a variety of appetites. The cop only buys donuts

- 32 machine upgrades: neon signs, cooling, tip jars

- 69 feats that unlock venues, product bundles, upgrades, cabinet skins, and color themes

- Seeded runs (type in a seed, get the exact same run) and auto saves after every decision

- Full controller support

Running a machine means dealing with everything that can, and often does, go wrong. Slots jam, Cooling fails, and overnight break-ins cost you stock. Each venue brings its own trouble: rats at the zoo, pickpockets working the stadium crowd, power cuts at the aquarium. Weather can influence the day too. Storms and heat waves are forecast a day ahead, so you can plan and restock around them; card skimmers and tax audits happen with no warning. Every problem needs a decision: pay a technician to fix it right away, or repair it yourself for free while that part of the machine stays out of action for two days.

Occasionally you'll be offered a second vending machine at a new venue. Take on the extra contract, or decline and stay focused on the one you have.

No microtransactions. No real gambling. Just honest vending.

About the demo: The demo contains four-week runs at four venues, with a reduced product lineup. No breakdowns, no second machines, and progress doesn't carry into the full game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dodge your way through three brutal levels of deadly enemies (and lasers) that kill you in an instant. Collect diamonds until you have enough to make it out alive. Can you dodge your way past everything and take down the final boss?

Dodge All the Things is a challenging single-player dodge 'em up, which is completely free due to its small scope. I hope the ratio of players rage-quitting to players finding joy in overcoming a hard challenge will not be too bad.

Although there are no in-game instructions for how to use a controller, you should be able to use an Xbox or Playstation controller just fine. With either the d-pad or left analog stick for movement, B/Circle for reset, and Menu/Options/Start for going back to the menu.

store_data.about_the_game:
Hellscum Tactics features tactical turn-based battles centered on squad building and development while exploring dungeons. 

Help the unjustly condemned escape from hell.

The player must choose four hellspawn and utilize their unique abilities and tactics to defeat enemies in turn-based battles.

Between battles, the player levels up the characters by selecting new skills and boosting their stats.

The player must manage risk when choosing the paths to escape hell.

The hellspawn's health does not regenerate between battles, so the player must rely on healing potions found along the way and random events.

Game features:

-Choose a team of hellspawn with unique abilities and help them escape from hell.

-Combat is tactical and turn-based, featuring grid-based movement and a strong emphasis on utilizing abilities.

-Use flanking and backstabs to increase damage.

-Gain experience, level up your team, choose new skills, and upgrade existing ones.

-Use crowd control abilities.

-Defeat bosses and complete special tasks to unlock more hellspawn.

store_data.about_the_game:
You have some money and a lot of opinions. Time to prove you're right.

Venture Capital Tycoon is a deep, systems-driven management sim about building a VC firm from a co-working hot desk to a name every founder knows. Start with your own small checkbook — no LPs, no fees, no safety net — and turn conviction into carry.

SELECT YOUR STARTUPS
Deal flow hits your inbox every week: AI wrappers, climate moonshots, crypto casinos, dentist software. Assign diligence, read the memo, weigh conviction against your dry powder — then wire the check or pass. Every pass is remembered: the anti-portfolio immortalizes the ones that got away.

BUILD THE FIRM
Hire partners, analysts, and the CFO who signs everything when you flip on autopilot. Every hire is a personality with stats and traits — build out your dream team, organize them into deal squads, and put the right specialists on the right deals. Upgrade from a hot desk to the corner office. Manage burn, court LPs, and raise Fund I, II, and beyond — each fund bigger, each miss more expensive.

TAKE THE RISK
Most of your portfolio goes to zero. That's the business. What matters is the one that doesn't: the 50x grand slam, the unicorn at a billion-dollar mark, the IPO that returns the fund. Follow on into your winners, sell into acquisition offers, or hold and pray.

THREE WAYS TO PLAY
Classic Firm (the full journey, Easy through Brutal), The Bootstrapper (hardest mode: one backer, $1M, a 1 in every stat, completely alone), and Empire Mode (skip the grind — start at scale with $100M and a full senior team).

A LEGACY WORTH KEEPING
Every completed run earns Legend points to spend on your next firm. Climb the all-time leaderboard, outrank the big firms, or — one day — take the whole firm public.

  • New game+ legacy system across runs

  • No microtransactions. The only carried interest is in the game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Let's cut to the chase…

Packs To Riches is a dangerously satisfying card-collecting incremental where a steady hand beats good luck, and a fortune is one clean cut away.

Work through a growing shelf of sealed product, each with its own rules, surprises, and ways to burn you. Slice packs open by hand, watch the condition of what is inside ride on how well you do it, and send your best cards off to be graded and slabbed at a perfect 10.

Unlock the auto opener, your tireless mechanical friend who tears through packs while you sit back and count the money. Just be careful what you feed it. It cuts the same careless way every time, and it has never once produced a perfect card.

Cut. Grade. Repeat.

As the money comes in, you will unlock upgrades that tilt the whole operation in your favour:

  • Sharper scissors and a steadier hand

  • Better odds, fatter payouts, faster grading

  • New pack formats with completely new rules

But the good stuff always bites. Brittle nineties vintage that tears if you breathe on it. Water-damaged lots holding cards that cost you money the moment you flip them. Resealed fakes that look perfect until you know what to look for. Will you open packs like a professional, or tear in like a kid on Christmas morning?

Going once, going twice…

When you are ready, sell the entire collection and start again. Bank your contacts, spend them on permanent upgrades, and unlock the parts of the hobby you could never reach before: the auction house, sealed vintage cases, and binders where every single card is a flawless 10.

Packs To Riches is a card shop incremental with a real skill at the heart of it, where every pack is a small gamble, and every perfect cut is one card closer to the collection of a lifetime!

Momentum Based Movement

Chain together parkour abilities to overcome platforming challenges, and reach new heights! Combat is speed-preserving and centered around quickly eliminating foes.

Colorful Handcrafted World

Make your way through sunny streets, soaring airships, underground gardens, and a city in the clouds. Become familiar with exciting new areas as you overcome their challenges and figure out their layouts, until you can fly through them with ease. Everything is created by hand, and each area has its own unique feeling and aesthetic.

  • Momentum based puzzles

  • Energetic, melody forward soundtrack

  • Unlockable outfits

  • Optional time-trial challenges

store_data.about_the_game:
🏙️ BUILD YOUR OWN SKYSCRAPER


Start with a small building and develop it floor by floor into a massive skyscraper.

Plan the layout, decide on the use of each floor and combine apartments, offices, shops, leisure facilities and hotels into a functioning building complex.

You decide how your tower grows and what story it tells.

🛗 PLAN EFFICIENT TRAFFIC ROUTES


Thousands of residents, office workers, visitors and hotel guests need to reach their destinations reliably every day.

Plan elevators, stairs, entrances and lobbies so that people can move through your tower quickly and without long waiting times.

Prevent overcrowded areas, identify bottlenecks and adapt the traffic routes to the growth of your building.

🍽️ FULFILL PEOPLE'S NEEDS


Every group of people in your tower has their own requirements.

Residents want to live comfortably, office workers need a functioning work environment, visitors look for shopping and entertainment, while hotel guests place particular value on service and comfort.

Set up suitable facilities and services:

  • Snack bars and restaurants
  • Shops and service providers
  • Cinemas and leisure facilities
  • Ballrooms and event spaces
  • Further amenities for daily needs

Make sure that the right services are available in the right place and that the needs of all groups of people are met.

Only when residents, office workers, visitors and hotel guests feel comfortable can your tower be successful in the long term.

🏨 BUILD AND ORGANIZE YOUR OWN HOTEL


Integrate a hotel into your skyscraper and ensure smooth operations.

Plan hotel rooms, receptions, restaurants and other service areas. Make sure your guests can check in quickly, reach their rooms and are well looked after during their stay.

A well-organized hotel brings new visitors and additional revenue to your tower.

🗑️ ENSURE CLEANLINESS IN THE TOWER


Where many people live and work, a large amount of waste is produced every day.

Plan an efficient waste management system, organize disposal and prevent garbage from piling up in your building.

Place waste collection points sensibly, optimize transport routes and ensure that apartments, offices, restaurants and public areas remain clean.

A clean tower increases the satisfaction of its residents, employees, guests and visitors.

🚨 ENSURE SECURITY IN THE TOWER


The larger your building becomes, the more important security and organization become.

Set up security centers, employ suitable personnel and respond to disruptions and unexpected events.

Monitor critical areas and ensure that residents, guests, visitors and employees are protected at all times.

📊 KEEP AN EYE ON YOUR BALANCE SHEETS


Every new floor and every facility incurs costs.

Monitor your income and expenses, plan investments and decide when the right time for the next expansion has come.

  • Manage rental income and operating costs
  • Invest in new floors and facilities
  • Optimize unprofitable areas
  • Develop your tower into a successful business

Build smart, fulfill people's needs and create a skyscraper that never stands still.

YOUR TOWER. YOUR DECISIONS. YOUR STORY.

store_data.about_the_game:
Two games, one idea.

Luminko is a match-3 puzzle that feeds a physics-driven pachinko payout, wrapped in a roguelite of tiles, ball loadouts, and a fate-navigated map. First you build the board by matching. Then you break it — raining your loadout of balls through the pegs you just made for a score that snowballs out of control.

You are a lamplighter, travelling town to town. Charge the crystals, string the lights across the houses, and dispel the darkness that caps each town. Clear it, and the town shines.

[h2]Build, then break[/h2]

  • A single persistent board carries through your whole run — you compound it, you never restart it.

  • Spend your moves matching 3+ crystals: merged crystals rise a level and score exponentially more.

  • Then drop your ball loadout. Every peg and tile it touches pays out. A smart merge now is a jackpot later.

[h2]No two runs play alike[/h2]

Buy from the townsfolk between matches and your whole playstyle changes:

  • 30 fairies — 15 common, 10 rare, and 5 event-only legendaries — that orbit your board and bend the rules: magnets, midas coins, phoenix revivals, chain-lightning, and more.

  • 36 tiles — special pegs from splash detonations to greed engines, including 5 legendary "grow cards" that start small and snowball the longer you keep them.

  • 30 balls — a loadout deck across common, rare, and legendary tiers, plus 3 editions (Gilded, Radiant, Prismatic) that add a shine on top of the ball's own trick.

  • 11 events — risk/reward encounters on the map: wishing wells, enchanters, cursed bargains, ember altars. Push your luck or play it safe.

A climb to the boss

Every run is a 12-level branching climb. Each level is its own procedural winter town; a boss caps every third one. Bosses are known in advance, so your shopping has direction — buy to beat the rule you can see coming. Light all four towns and topple the final boss to win the run.

One miss away

Miss a level's target and the run ends immediately — back to a fresh board. Roguelite stakes, not casual comfort. Every ball counts.

Cozy on the outside

Hand-drawn snow-capped villages, chimney smoke, a lamplighter tending the post, drifting snow, and a garland of lights that fills in as you clear each town. The reward isn't just a coin count — it's a dark town coming to light.

  • Full keyboard and gamepad support with on-screen button prompts, plus rumble.

  • Built to run great on Steam Deck and desktop.

store_data.about_the_game:
Kill Them All is a single-player game that combines party-based RPG combat, deckbuilding, and roguelike elements.

Lead three amnesiac adventurers who share a hand and Action Points. Make your choices before enemy countdowns reach zero. Collect cards, legendary weapons, and treasures, venture deep into the remnants of the Demon King's domain, reclaim your lost power, and kill everything that stands in your way.

Choose three characters from a cast with radically different combat styles and assemble your own party.

Each character has unique stats, cards, and progression paths. Some excel at taking hits, some heal allies, while others rely on critical strikes, poison, control, or special status effects to end battles.

All three characters share one deck, one hand, and one pool of Action Points. How you spend limited resources, when you protect an ally, and when you concentrate your strength on offense will determine how far the party can go.

Each character has 13 class cards and 2 Masterstroke cards, which together form their unique combat system.

Every class card offers 3 distinct upgrade paths. Depending on your party composition and build strategy, the same card can evolve into dramatically different effects: becoming the core of a character's build, covering a party weakness, or creating new synergies with other characters.

The game also includes 41 neutral cards. They belong to no specific class and can be freely added to the party deck, providing new tools for an existing strategy or forming the foundation of an entirely new archetype.

Choose different cards and upgrade paths to build a combat system truly your own under the shared-hand and shared-Action-Point rules.

Cards are only one part of your build.

Find and forge different weapons, equip treasures with unique effects, and carry consumables capable of turning the tide. Attack, Spirit, Critical Rate, and many other combat stats all change with your equipment.

A legendary weapon can completely transform how a character fights, while an unassuming treasure may become the heart of an entire archetype. Combine cards, equipment, and treasures to create a different progression path on every journey.

Enemies will not stand quietly and wait for your turn to end.

Every action pushes their countdowns closer to zero. The moment a countdown reaches zero, that enemy acts immediately. Read enemy intentions, control the order of your actions, and kill, interrupt, or disable them before they can strike.

When an ally falls, they do not immediately leave the battle. That character's cards transform into rescue actions, forcing you to choose between pressing the attack and bringing your companion back.

Pass through unknown events, dangerous elites, and powerful enemies waiting at the end of the road.

Enter their territory. Leave none alive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Run. Adapt. Push Your Limits.

Enter a synthwave universe where neon lights and futuristic colors set the stage for a challenge built around absolute precision.

In Geometry Run, you control a glowing cube in a 3D third-person platformer where every jump, every landing, and every second can make the difference. The path to the finish line is easy to understand, but difficult to master.

Whether you want to complete every level or chase the perfect time, the challenge remains the same: become faster than your previous run.

Built for Speedrunners

Every level is designed to be replayed dozens of times. Discover shortcuts, perfect your routes, eliminate unnecessary movements, and constantly improve your time.

The mechanics are easy to learn but require precision, memory, and reflexes to master. Every mistake becomes an opportunity to find a more efficient path and transform a good run into a perfect one.

Three Ways to Play Every Level

Each level offers three different variations:

Normal

Experience the original route and learn the obstacles, rhythm, and mechanics.

Reverse

Replay the level in the opposite direction. The entire route changes, and everything you learned must be rethought from scratch.

Time Trial

A mode designed to push your skills to the limit. Faster, more intense, and made for those searching for the perfect run.

A Neon World

Immerse yourself in a synthwave-inspired aesthetic featuring vibrant colors, neon lights, futuristic environments, and an electronic soundtrack that accompanies every moment of your run.

The minimalist style keeps the action clear and focused, allowing you to concentrate on what truly matters: the next jump.

Every run is a new attempt.
Every attempt is a new record to beat.

store_data.about_the_game:
A KINGDOM CONSUMED BY DARKNESS

Once, the Kingdom of Elaris stood against the Abyss King. In a desperate attempt to seal him away, a forbidden ritual was performed using the power of the Shadow Flame—but the ritual failed.

The kingdom fell, five ancient hearts were scattered across corrupted realms, and Shadow was sealed within the ruins.

Years later, awakened by a mysterious wizard, Shadow must reclaim the five lost hearts, confront the guardians twisted by the Abyss, and uncover the truth behind the fall of Elaris.

MASTER THE POWER OF SHADOW

Fight through a variety of corrupted enemies using fast melee combat and unlockable shadow abilities. Adapt your powers to each encounter, break through enemy defenses, and discover new ways to survive increasingly dangerous battles.

EXPLORE SIX DARK-FANTASY REALMS

Journey across six distinct handcrafted worlds, from forgotten ruins and haunted forests to crystal dimensions, volcanic kingdoms, corrupted sanctuaries, and a royal palace suspended within the void.

Each realm introduces its own atmosphere, enemies, environmental dangers, platforming challenges, puzzles, and powerful boss encounters.

FACE POWERFUL GUARDIANS

Every lost heart is protected by a deadly guardian. Learn their attack patterns, avoid devastating abilities, and strike during moments of vulnerability. Each confrontation tests your movement, timing, and mastery of Shadow’s abilities.

UNCOVER A FORGOTTEN TRUTH

Discover memories, ancient ruins, and fragments of a fallen kingdom’s history. As Shadow moves closer to the Abyss King, the true purpose of the ritual—and the identity of the one responsible for its failure—begins to emerge.

KEY FEATURES

  • Atmospheric 2D action-adventure set in a dark-fantasy world

  • Fast-paced melee combat and unlockable shadow powers

  • Six distinct realms with unique environments and challenges

  • Platforming, exploration, environmental hazards, and puzzles

  • Powerful multi-phase boss battles

  • Cinematic story sequences and lore-driven storytelling

  • Full controller-focused gameplay

  • An original journey created by solo developer Black Dune Studio

The five hearts are waiting. Reclaim them, uncover the truth, and decide the fate of the Dead Lands.

Revolver 21 is a narrative card game set in the context of the Soviet Union during World War II.

store_data.about_the_game:
Concept

In each game you receive a pool of random tiles that you should place on a blank board to create a map. Every tile can be rotated freely and contains a random arrangement of mountains, forests, meadows, swamps, water, buildings, or settlements.

Each settlement gathers resources from its own buildings and from surrounding terrain: fields provide food, mountains provide production, and water provides both food and gold. Settlements also collect resources from buildings, animals, and ships connected to them via roads, rivers, or coastlines.

Food allows a settlement to grow by adding new buildings. Production allows upgrades to existing buildings. Gold goes into a general pool. Each settlement also has a range that determines how far its influence extends. Different buildings have different construction costs and produce different resources. The entire process of growth and upgrading is automated in the basic version of the game.

Drawing

Terrain tiles are placed on a hex‑based grid. In addition, you can freely draw individual mountains, forests, trees, meadows, swamps, buildings, settlements, animals, water segments, roads, rivers, or labels anywhere on the map. Every drawing has a gold cost. Almost all map elements are animated to imitate the process of hand‑drawing - the entire map gradually appears before your eyes in real time.

Folks (Races)

The game will feature 23 playable folks (races or species). Each will have its own map frame, emblem, and unique graphics for all buildings. Each folk will also have special buildings that provide unique resources or functions. They also have special traits (for example, Dwarves gain extra gold from mountains and have a production bonus) and their own sets of prefixes and suffixes for generating names of villages, cities, mountain ranges, etc.

States (Countries)

You can place one or more states on the map, in any color. A state may consist of a single folk, but multiple folks can coexist within it. Likewise, each settlement may contain several ethnic minorities alongside its main people.

In addition to basic resources, settlements also generate strength, produced for example by castles and watchtowers. Strength influences state borders and contributes to conquests - the takeover of settlements from one state by another.

Experience

In the game, you earn experience, levels, and ranks. Experience comes from completing a map as well as from fulfilling tasks during its creation. These tasks may ask you to draw, for example, a forest of a certain size, a settlement with a specific population, or a state of a particular area.

Tasks have levels - higher levels demand more but grant better rewards. Rewards include extra experience, tiles, gold, or drawings. In the basic version of the game you start with only one people and a few basic drawings (mountains, water segments, buildings). Everything else is unlocked gradually by completing tasks on new maps. New folks are also unlocked as high‑level task rewards.

Current Progress

At the moment I have completed 5 out of 23 planned folks:
• Albins - humans inspired by Medieval Europe
• Erabs - humans inspired by Greek, Persian, and Arabian cultures
• Barbarians - humans inspired by Norse and Scottish traditions
• Jin-Hans - humans inspired by Mongolian, Chinese and Japanese cultures
• Enuits - humans inspired by Inuit culture
The remaining 18 are waiting - including dwarves, elves, halflings, orcs, and many more.

Many planned features are already functional, while several modes and systems are still in development. I'm currently working on the Steam video trailer and a climate system that affects the appearance and resources of forests and fields.

I don't have a release date yet, but I plan to launch the first playable version once the game reaches 10–12 folks. Additional folks will be added later as free updates, and I don't intend to release them as paid DLC. There will also be no microtransactions in the game.

store_data.about_the_game:
One kitchen. Ten hours. Four cooks who won't stop moving the stove.

Tiny Chef is a co-op restaurant management game. You open the doors, customers sit down, and from that moment you are behind. Chop, fry, plate, run it to the table, take the next order on the way back. Somewhere in there the fryer catches fire and nobody has washed a plate since Tuesday.

Play alone, on one couch, or online with up to four people.

The shift

Every day runs on a real clock. Demand rises and falls with the hour, so the lunch rush is a different game than the dead stretch at 3pm. Customers arrive alone or in parties of up to four, sit together, order together, and lose patience together. Serve the table late and the whole party walks.

Nothing about the kitchen is fixed. Pick up the chopping board and carry it somewhere better. Buy a second stove off your phone and wait two days for the truck. Fires spread to the next counter if you don't get there in time.

The rest of the day

The shift is only part of it. Between services you drive back to HQ, sleep until whatever hour you choose, and spend the money you made:

  • Order appliances and gadgets by phone and unload the delivery truck yourself

  • Learn new dishes and decide which ones stay on the menu

  • Run ad campaigns to pull in more customers than you can handle

  • Hire contractors to knock out walls, move doors and rebuild the floor plan

  • Buy the empty lot next door and grow the building into it

  • Book a cleaning crew when you really do not want to face the sink

Do well enough and you open a second restaurant. Then a third. Fail enough orders in one day and the health inspector shuts one down, and reopening costs more the longer you've been running.

Your cook is yours

Make a character, pick their face and clothes, and take them anywhere. Skills go from 1 to 99 and only go up by doing the work. Chop a thousand onions and you chop faster. Fight enough fires and you stop being scared of the fryer. Your  character carries that progress into any save and into anyone else's game.

Co-op that actually shares the kitchen

Online through Steam, or two players on one screen with controllers. Everyone cooks, everyone can buy things, everyone can move the furniture while you're standing on it. There is one phone and whoever grabbed it first is using it.

Also, there is a bed and a car

You have to drive to work. You have to sleep. You will, at some point, open the restaurant and immediately be told you cannot start the shift because there is one dirty plate on a table. That one is on you.

A package was delivered to your house by mistake. The address on the package is in another country, so you set out to return it in person, well, in dog (you are a dog).

The country turns out to be a strange place. People (dogs) there settle everything with target-shooting duels. Nobody finds this odd except you.

The trick is the ricochet: bullets bounce off walls, so the best shots are the ones that look impossible until they land. Hitting targets shakes your opponent's confidence.

Along the way you travel with a cat who was raised by dogs and firmly believes she is one. You meet the locals, run into trouble, help random grandma, and sort most of it out with a well-placed bank shot.

Features

  • A very fun story

  • Meet random dogs (well, mostly) along the way

  • Pretty scene

  • Full controller support

  • Interesting levels

store_data.about_the_game:
Books for Bad Neighbors

It's 199X. This is the only bookshop for forty miles, and you work the counter now. The register is old, the computer screen glows orange, and the mail comes every day whether you want it or not.

A priest hears the confession. A doctor sees the wound. You get a list of what they read at two in the morning, and it tells you more than both of them put together.

The work is simple

Order new books every day. Read the letters. Find the books you have. Pack the boxes. Hit your quota, close the shop. Then do it again tomorrow.

What the supplier sells changes every week, and some books sell out and never come back, so what you can give people is not always your choice.

Fill enough orders for one person and their letters get longer. They start telling you things. By then you've read enough of their mail to finish their sentences.

Some orders you should not fill

You still have a quota to hit, and if you say no to someone, they will want to know why, and they know where you work.

The shop closes at six. You walk home the same way every night.

Features

  • Multiple mysteries to uncover, one order at a time

  • Different endings based on what you sold and who you sold it to

  • Everything happens on the shop computer, built to feel like a real 199X machine

store_data.about_the_game:
Miners, Moos & Miracles is an idle/incremental farm-and-adventure game with a retro CRT-styled shell.

Start with a modest homestead and watch gold, barley, milk, and eggs roll in while you're away. Reinvest your earnings, then step through the door into a handful of wildly different mini-games, all set in the same strange little world:

  • Dark Mine — send your miners underground to battle demons for shards, upgrading equipment, dynamite, and hydraulics along the way.

  • Cooking — combine eggs, milk, seeds, fish, and a few less wholesome ingredients into dozens of recipes, from a Simple Stew to a full-blown Reincarnation Ritual.

  • Cow Ball — the barnyard's favorite sport. Exactly what it sounds like.

  • Chicken Coop — keep the flock happy, then fend off egg-snatching UFOs in the coop's Space Invasion mode.

  • Aquarium — feed and grow fish in the homestead.

  • Wardrobe — customize your character's look.

When you've pushed as far as you can, Rebirth: reset your progress for a permanent bonus, a growing skill tree, and a merchant who'll trade your hard-earned resources for Prestige Points.

Over 50 achievements track your progress across every resource and mini-game plus a few one-off moments worth catching, if you're paying attention.

Feature list

  • Idle/incremental homestead management: miners, farms, houses, cows, and more

  • Six distinct mini-games in one shared world: Dark Mine, Cooking, Cow Ball, Chicken Coop, Aquarium, and Wardrobe

  • A full Rebirth/Prestige system with a skill tree and permanent bonuses

  • Over 50 Steam achievements, from resource milestones to one-off surprises

  • A retro CRT-styled UI shell with scanlines, bezel themes, and screen effects

  • Multiple endings, including route endings, bad endings, and clues toward a deeper hidden truth.

The game contains satire, romance, comedy, and light social themes, but no explicit adult content.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dunjin

The Dunjin. You'd heard the name whispered. Heard the stories. But nothing prepared you for what waits in the dark - something old, something patient, something that's spent centuries reshaping the world above it to its will. Every floor you descend, you feel it. Watching. Waiting. And now it knows you're coming.

Play your hand, then roll your fate

Dunjin fuses poker-hand deckbuilding with dice-driven dungeon crawling. Build hands from a deck of sigil-marked cards to generate Mana and Mult, then let the d20 decide whether your hit lands, fumbles, or strikes for a crit. Your cards are only half the story down here, but they can easily make or break your run. Here's how it works.

Four sigils, one descent

Every card bears one of four sigils - Divine, Arcane, Martial, and Shadow - each enabling different strategies and synergies in battle. Divine heals you up, Arcane breaks shields, Martial melts HP, and Shadow shreds armor.

Damage is compounded by the strength of your hand. Rig the deck towards your favourite sigil, the relics you find, or even a hand type you have a keen eye for (looking at you, flushmaxxers).

24 classes: no two runs alike

From the stalwart Knight to the humble Rat King, every hero descends with a different set of perks and passives. Some load the dice, others rig the deck. No two heroes play the same, and each one is uniquely equipped to get you the upper-hand on your journey.

Dungeons with stories untold

store_data.about_the_game:
Descend. Loot. Escape — or lose it all.

Depths of Providence is a roguelike JRPG inspired by the Ancient Cave of Lufia II. Every run drops your four-hero party at floor 1, level 1, with nothing but the relics you've banked from previous descents. One hundred procedurally generated floors stand between you and the Guardian of the Depths. What you carry out is yours forever, but only if you make it out.

Every run is a gamble. Red chests hold run-only gear, consumables, and spell scrolls to keep you alive right now. Blue chests hold rare named equipment; escape with them and they're banked in your vault forever, ready at the start of every future run. Somewhere on floors 15–24, a single glowing Providence chest lets you end the run from anywhere and keep everything you've found. Cash out early and bank little, or push deeper and risk it all. Die, and everything you found this run is gone.

The deep floors are unfair on purpose. Instant-death gazes, petrification, and full-party nukes await the greedy. Death wards, white magic, and knowing when to run are the difference between a full vault and an empty one. Every tenth floor a mini-boss guards the stairs, and floor 100 belongs to Chrono-Lord Aiful himself: slay him and your haul is banked and forged into a super-blue, a relic with a unique, randomly generated affix all your own.

Secrets run deeper still. Rumor speaks of eight Ancient Key shards scattered through blue chests. Complete the key and bring it to the cave's depths, and something older opens

Compete on the Daily. Everyone descends the same seeded cave each day. Same floors, same chests, same formations, and races for depth on a global leaderboard. Every run is replay-verified, so the board is real.

Features:

  • 100 procedurally generated floors with escalating, deliberately punishing depths

  • Persistent vault: bank rare blue-chest relics across every future run

  • The Providence mechanic: a genuine risk/reward "cash out or push on" decision every run

  • Turn-based JRPG battle with classes, spells, elemental affinities, and 11 equipment slots

  • Named super-blue relics forged with unique procedural affixes

  • Hidden Ancient Key questline and an unlockable custom Party Builder

  • Daily seeded runs with a global, replay-verified leaderboard

  • Full controller support, Steam Deck ready

A Personal Note from the Developer:

The above is all accurate, but it's ostensibly the typical marketing hype one might read for a game. I wanted to tell you the brutally honest truth about why I made this game, and why I think you might enjoy it. I really enjoy JRPG's. My biggest complaint about them has always been that they're too easy. Some might have moments that are challenging, others may start a bit difficult but pretty soon the player just stat checks everything and it's a snooze. The game I always have wanted is a turn based JRPG with a high skill cap, near infinite replayability, and a competitive aspect. That game, as far as I am aware, does not exist, so I set out to make it.

The story mode of the game is cool. One basically tries to go as deep as possible to acquire as many powerful blue chest items as they can before they escape the Depths via Providence. There's real tension between pushing deeper or getting out with what you can. The player is not supposed to make it to floor 100 on the first run. I think this mode is fun, but it isn't really the primary mode I built this game for, though if you are someone who loves meta-progression, stacking mountains of obscenely powerful items, then you might love this mode forever.

The other mode is the daily challenge run. This run has no meta-progression. You start from level 1 on floor 1 with no skills and no banked items. You and everyone else face the same procedurally generated Depths on any given day; same enemy formations, same chest contents, same skill drops, and same blue chest items. This mode is fine-tuned with increased blue chest occurrence such that with near perfect play, and a little bit of luck, a player might hope to make it deep, but the overwhelming majority of players will probably die off at floor 20-something. There's a daily leaderboard to track who makes it the deepest on any given day and there's server side replay validation of every submitted run so that players can be assured of fair play. This mode is why I built this game, and I promise to always tune this to be fiendishly difficult so that if you can pull off a deep run, it'll be something to really be proud of.

Anyway, I truly hope you enjoy this game as much as I do. I'm honestly not expecting huge commercial success from this endeavor; I just want to share my work with others in the hopes that some of you might enjoy the game as much as I do. My heartfelt thanks for considering purchasing my game.

Desperate for Success

Twin brothers Bennet and Chase are small-time streamers who bake pastries. Despite great effort, they struggle to attract viewers.

PaleGlucose17: u shud put an apple on his head

Desperate, the twin brothers adopt a new approach to reach Internet fame. Through increasingly reckless William Burroughs-inspired stunts, they begin to garner interest from the online community, but their growing viewer count only seems to worsen the brothers' unbearable rivalry.

Mackbeth33: yo the blue pajama guy is weird

You play as Chase Alden, quiet twin brother to the beloved and charismatic Bennet. Internet fame gives Chase a newfound confidence and intensifies his jealousy, making him more and more difficult to control.

GirlGeorge922: Ong so much scripted content these days...this stream is jankyy

Can a fertilized egg split after birth? Can Chase find the inner strength to break away on his own? Will he silently endure his brother until he cracks? Chase's emotional state unravels, and the player must aim to control his conscience against growing fantasies of killing his brother.

Behind the Camera

Help you and your twin reach internet fame by performing life-threatening stunts on stream. Between stunts, you also stream the cooking and delve further into the twins' strange world.

Stunts
Your player character's state interferes with your aim. Aim carefully and find the right timing. Right-click to briefly steady your aim. The window is short so act quickly while the crosshair turns green.Right-click, flick, and shoot almost immediately. You can miss but try not to shoot Bennet.

Passion for pastry 
Sometimes it's not about shooting the apple it's about shooting the show.

Disclaimer:

The stunts in this game are fictional and performed by reckless amateurs. Do not attempt them in real life.

store_data.about_the_game:
Stop time. Hang the bullets. Remember to step aside.

You're the only thing moving in a frozen world. A bullet hovers eight inches from your face. A grenade sits motionless mid-arc. A crowd of dummies stands there, mouths open - and you have all the time in the world to decide what happens to them.

Shoot, and your bullets hang in the air. Throw grenades, and they stay exactly where you left them. Shove enemies around, line them up in each other's crossfire, tuck their own explosives back into their hands. Then let time run - and watch it all happen at once.

You're not hitting pause. You're staging a scene.

Freezing time isn't a breather here, it's a director's chair. Build a thirty-bullet volley. Rig a chain reaction: bullet hits boulder, boulder launches a dummy, dummy sails into a crowd with a grenade already waiting in it. Unfreezing time is your "Action!"

And yes, you're standing right in the middle of it.

This is a first-person shooter, and your body is part of the plan. The bullet you parked by the doorway doesn't care who parked it there. The shockwave you forgot to hide behind will find you first. Before you let time run, there's one question left: where do you stand to survive your own masterpiece?

Your dummies come straight out of myth

Sling-swinging satyrs. Harpies raining feather-darts mid-dive. Cyclopes lobbing smoldering boulders. Bronze guardians behind tower shields. A gorgon whose gaze petrifies anything it lands on - including her own allies, if you nudge them into the beam. And eventually, you'll meet the ones who can stop time too. That's when it becomes a real duel.

What's inside:

  • Sandbox - one arena, the full arsenal, zero rules. Build Rube Goldberg machines, shoot movies, break physics.

  • Challenges - dozens of levels with brutal conditions: one bullet for five enemies, one freeze for the whole level, everyone dies in a single volley.

  • Style scoring - shooting a dummy point-blank earns you nothing. A five-link chain, an enemy killed by his own redirected bullet, a kill pulled off an inch from your own death - that earns you everything.

  • Replays - every cascade is recorded and replayed from a free camera. The first time you'll see yourself from the outside, standing in the middle of the hell you built. One click to save the clip.

  • Ragdolls, explosions, and a total absence of dignity - the dummies have none. Neither will you, when the plan goes wrong.

Time is stopped. The bullets are waiting. Sure you thought this through?

Rip N Ship is a card-streaming simulator where you build a following, open packs for viewers, manage live orders, and turn a basement setup into a full rip-and-ship operation.

Start with a simple desk, a small collection, and barely anyone watching. Go live, grow your audience, take pack orders, work through the queue, react to big pulls, and keep viewers entertained while you build your reputation as a card breaker.

Streamer Mode brings the whole experience together with simulated live chat, viewer activity, followers, subscriptions, tips, raids, purchases, alerts, giveaways, auctions, and customer orders. Display slabs from your personal collection, choose one for a giveaway or auction, and run the event directly from your stream setup.

Outside the stream, collect cards, organize your binder, manage duplicates and bulk, grade your best pulls, sell cards, unlock new stages, and improve your setup as your channel grows.

This Early Access build includes:

store_data.about_the_game:
A mysterious corruption is spreading across the region, twisting the minds of every creature it touches. Assemble a team of animal survivors, uncover the source behind the outbreak, and fight your way through ever-changing runs where every battle, card and Artifact shapes your strategy.

Command Three Survivors

Every battle is fought by a team of three survivors, each with their own deck, strengths and combat role. The entire party shares a single Action Point pool, so every card played is a choice between offense, defense and supporting your teammates. Success comes from coordinating the whole team rather than relying on a single character.

Every Character Brings a Different Strategy

Each survivor contributes to the team in a different way. Sharp Bengal overwhelms enemies with relentless offense, Pirate Albino supports the fight through gadgets and calculated precision, while Boss Shepherd keeps the team alive with powerful defensive abilities. Experiment with different team compositions to discover powerful strategies that no single character could achieve alone.

Survive the Corruption

The corruption is as dangerous as the enemies themselves. Each survivor has a Stagger meter. When it fills, they become Broken, losing their next turn and becoming vulnerable to devastating attacks. Most defensive cards allow another survivor to Intercept an incoming attack, stepping in to take the hit instead. Knowing when to protect an ally—and when to risk pushing forward—can decide the outcome of an entire battle.

Build Three Decks

Each survivor builds their own deck throughout the run. Draft new cards, upgrade existing ones and discover powerful Artifacts that reshape your strategy. Every addition strengthens an individual character while creating new synergies across the entire team, making every run feel different.

Explore a Corrupted Region

Travel through corrupted Zones filled with dangerous enemies, unpredictable Events, powerful Elites and terrifying Bosses. Every route presents different risks and rewards, encouraging you to adapt your strategy as the corruption grows stronger.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build Your Own Restaurant Empire

Start with a small restaurant and gradually grow it into a thriving food business. In Woks & Works, you will not only design your restaurant layout and create menus, but also manage employees, control inventory, plan supply chains, and respond to ever-changing customer demands.

Manage the Complete Production Chain, From Supply to Service

Every dish goes through a complete process:

  • Purchase fresh ingredients

  • Manage warehouse storage

  • Organize kitchen production

  • Assign tasks to employees

  • Serve customer orders

Plan your resources carefully and keep your restaurant running efficiently.

Every Customer Has Their Own Story

Customers come from different social classes, with unique incomes, spending habits, and dining preferences.

Students, workers, office employees, and wealthy customers will choose different dishes, shaping your business strategy. Understand your customers and build the restaurant that fits the market.

Manage Your Team

Chefs, servers, and other workers will act according to assigned tasks.

Organize your workforce, improve efficiency, and transform your restaurant from a chaotic small shop into a finely tuned business machine.

Design Your Restaurant Freely

Plan your kitchen, dining areas, warehouses, and workspaces.

Optimize your layout, reduce unnecessary movement, and create an efficient food production line of your own.

Adapt to a Changing Economy

Ingredient prices, market demand, and customer spending power will affect your business.

Adjust your menu, control costs, and find your path to success in a competitive restaurant industry.

Endless Possibilities

You can choose to:

  • Build a luxurious fine dining restaurant

  • Run an affordable neighborhood restaurant

  • Create an ultra-efficient automated kitchen

  • Build a massive restaurant empire

Your restaurant, your decisions.

store_data.about_the_game:
Ascend the Pixel Dungeon is a turn-based dungeon crawler.

The controls feel familiar — but this is not a game about picking a class tree and growing into it. You define how you fight with spellbooks, reshape your body with factors, and let maps and choices split every run apart.

The first door does not always open onto the same sewers. Some runs begin in a humid jungle. Segmented monsters that choke corridors, theme bosses at the end of a biome, spellbooks from bosses and chests — the question becomes which book you push for this time.

Defeat monsters and you may find factors. Absorb them and adaptations take hold. These are not simple stat buffs. Vision, hunger, equipment limits, and combat rules change — how your body lives in the dungeon changes. If spellbooks are how you fight, adaptations are the body that endures that fight.

Between chapters, a bonfire waits. Combine materials. Choose a material and forge weapons and armor. Start as a race — human or gnoll — face monsters that wear gear, and turn what they drop into the next decision.

Each run splits along those lines: starting biome, books in hand, body you absorbed, materials you forged. Learn the rules once. Become a different body the next time.

Key Features

• Turn-based pixel-art dungeon crawling — one tile, one action

• Spellbook-driven builds — carry books in a run and invest level-up points into them

• Factors & adaptations — kill monsters, learn their bodies

• Runs that diverge from the start — sewers or jungle

• Theme bosses and guaranteed or random spellbooks — the nameplate of your strategy

• Bonfire crafting — recipes and material-based forging

• Race select — human or gnoll as different starting bodies

• Equipped monsters — tougher fights, drops that matter

Ascend the Pixel Dungeon is a fork built on Shattered Pixel Dungeon. The bones of the controls are familiar. The axes of growth and run divergence are rebuilt.

@AI is used in art, music, and code.

store_data.about_the_game:
Big Adventure is a story-driven adventure game made in a pixel-art style. The game is divided into two types of chapters - story chapters and additional chapters.

In the first chapter, the main character (Usach Stas) protects the Valley of Green Fields from its ruthless enemies - robots that have come to seize this wonderful and peaceful place, build factories, and rule the land. The main goal is to destroy the death machine and save the valley from disaster.

The hero’s arsenal includes a blaster that fires an unusual green substance with a limited supply. You can replenish it by picking up bottles, cans, or canisters scattered throughout the levels. If that’s not possible, use boxes. Or dynamite! Just don’t get too carried away. In some situations, boxes can also be useful for good purposes.

In the first additional chapter, the twins Tony and Bonnie, who live in the Sunny Savannah, were preparing for a quiet life away from the bustle of the city. Nothing seemed to be wrong until someone stole an important device capable of providing their home with energy for many, many years. They immediately set off in pursuit of the thief, overcoming obstacles, caves, and rocky cliffs along the way.
PLEASE NOTE: For full comfort and access to all control features, it is strongly recommended to use a full‑sized keyboard. Using compact models may limit the gaming experience.

The game also includes a level editor! To unlock it, you simply need to complete the first chapter. The editor offers a wide range of features: many objects, level and editor settings, hotkeys, and more, plus a built-in instruction guide.
Create your own levels and share them with other players in our communities!

store_data.about_the_game:
THE SURVEILLANCE METER IS THE REAL BOSS

The Black Stack is a sentient corporate megastructure that placed divinity behind a permission gate.

You are unauthorized.

Build a forbidden deck. Steal hardware. Compile one-shot exploits. Climb toward the process that wrote God - and decide how much evidence to leave behind.

Protocols raise TRACE, which persists between encounters and crosses PING, LOCK, PURGE, and TERMINAL thresholds. Each arms a new response. High Trace distorts the interface and enemy intent; at 100, one grace cycle precedes escalating nonlethal Integrity loss. Vent it - or turn surveillance into fuel.

COMPILE YOUR OWN VERSION

Choose from three playable identities, each with a distinct body, starting kit, card pool, and power:

  • VANTA // THE APOSTATE - disciplined Bandwidth and Trace control through OVERCLOCK.

  • THE ARCHON KERNEL - stolen authority that turns dangerous Trace into power.

  • THE COURIER - a script-runner whose exploit inventory drives the deck.

The catalog contains 503 card definitions: 496 playable protocols and seven hostile Status injections. Build across Attacks, Skills, Powers, and 60 dedicated WAGER protocols. The wider library adds 78 relics, 66 exploit scripts, 16 Divine elixirs, 12 Ultras, five Graft Cores, and 12 Machine God blessings.

POWER LEAVES A SIGNAL

Across 496 playable protocols and 172 relics, scripts, elixirs, and Ultras, dozens of engines are waiting to be discovered - and broken open.

Power earned through play is allowed to feel powerful. We do not flatten an engine merely because it became obscene. Your LOADOUT SIGNAL lets Intelligent difficulty read rarity, mastery, equipment, and graft investment, then scale the Stack around you. Prefer a ceiling? Select Capped response. Add one of three Audit contracts for greater resistance and rewards.

PHYSICAL COPIES. PERMANENT MASTERY.

Recover schematics, spend Salvage to compile as many physical copies as you can afford, and build a ten-card opening manifest for each identity. Removed starters return to your library.

  • Basic through Rare protocols reach level 3; Divine protocols reach level 4.

  • Rare capstones and every Divine rank fork permanently, so copies of one card can become different weapons.

  • Maxed cards gain animated mastery chrome and rarity-aware play effects.

  • Wager protocols turn coin calls, dice, loaded reels, Blackjack, and roulette into seeded combat engines with bespoke animations.

SIX ACTS TO ROOT TERMINUS

Climb a branching, seeded ascent through five atlases, then enter ROOT TERMINUS: a straight eight-layer procession toward Archon Prime and its Ascendant second body.

Face 81 hostile processes and 58 authored event definitions, including eight adaptive Forensic Processes.

  • Fight multi-enemy encounters with individual intents and direct targeting.

  • Hunt elite variants and confront bespoke authorities - including one you can negotiate with.

  • At Archon checkpoints, repair, vent, extract a prize, or continue deeper.

  • Use REVOCATION once per run to reject a filed death and return at 1 HP and 0 Trace. The enemy's exact Integrity, Block, status, form, and intent remain; every player card returns to the deck.

ACCEPT THE MANDATE - OR REVOKE IT

A forbidden offer can transform your identity and unlock THE MANDATE: a second six-act campaign that turns the route inside out and sends you against ten new authorities.

Protect the system you once breached, pursue older powers, or revoke your appointment and return to the oath. The Archive remembers which version chose.

THE STACK LEARNS HOW YOU FIGHT

Combat Doctrine records your openers, sequences, Bandwidth use, defense, targets, Trace appetite, wagers, and equipment. The Stack uses those habits in Forensic Processes - and when archived versions return.

Failed and strongest selves can rebuild their real deck, mastery branches, equipment, resources, piles, and learned doctrine. The most dangerous encounter may be the version that mastered your own engine first.

DESCEND BELOW THE STACK

A route can fracture into the DEEP BREACH, a rare once-per-run exception that suspends your exact atlas and opens an eight-stop illegal descent.

Three authorities. Two corrupted casinos. A Divine cache. An apex boss. Extraction.

Escape and the original atlas reconnects where it broke, contraband intact. Die below the Stack and the run ends. Complete a naturally filed descent to recover the secret Godscar Engine Graft Core.

THE BLACK ARCHIVE REMEMBERS EVERY VERSION

  • Recovery Catalog + Workbench - unlock and compile components, construct manifests, and master individual copies.

  • Graft Foundry - install one of five cores and commit to one of 15 doctrines across 150 authored nodes. Reset for a full Salvage refund.

  • The Ascent - infinite, non-seasonal progression. Complete twelve-node chapters for Gems and new deterministic reward lines.

  • Breach Archive + Memory Index - reopen run maps and telemetry; catalog encountered processes, origins, art, and lore.

  • NULLCADE - two permanent cabinets: BREACHEROIDS and the seven-stage NULLSPIRE, with persistent scores and bounded rewards.

THE HOUSE ALWAYS COLLECTS

Wager Dens select deterministic Blackjack or an animated 3x3 reel machine. Between runs, spend earned Gems at Big Six for XP, Salvage, property, or an unowned Divine protocol. Every stake uses fictional currency earned only through play.

ONE PRICE. THE COMPLETE GAME.

Everything here is included in one purchase and earned through play.

No microtransactions, paid currency, card packs, paid battle pass, loot boxes, real-money wagering, or cash-out.

SHARED RULES. YOUR DECISIONS.

  • Every run is deterministic; share a BREACH CODE to replay its route.

  • SCHEDULED AUDITS are seeded challenges with fixed identity, kit, route, and modifier.

  • A guided tutorial teaches combat, Trace, Block, the Archive, deck construction, mastery, grafts, and loadouts.

  • Save and resume route and combat state, with Steam Cloud reconciliation.

BUILT FOR THE WHOLE RUN

  • 60 Steam achievements and 31 interface languages.

  • Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad navigation.

  • Separate audio, display, atmosphere, post FX, shake, impact, and reduced-motion settings.

  • Card inspection, forecasts, reactive music, cinematics, hit-stop, shield fractures, kill dissolves, particles, and atmosphere.

The Stack is generating another version of you.

Failed and strongest selves can rebuild their real deck, mastery branches, equipment, resources, piles, and learned doctrine. The most dangerous encounter may be the version that mastered your own engine first.

DESCEND BELOW THE STACK

A route can fracture into the DEEP BREACH, a rare once-per-run exception that suspends your exact atlas and opens an eight-stop illegal descent.

Three authorities. Two corrupted casinos. A Divine cache. An apex boss. Extraction.

Escape and the original atlas reconnects where it broke, contraband intact. Die below the Stack and the run ends. Complete a naturally filed descent to recover the secret Godscar Engine Graft Core.

Wager Dens select deterministic Blackjack or an animated 3x3 reel machine. Between runs, spend earned Gems at Big Six for XP, Salvage, property, or an unowned Divine protocol. Every stake uses fictional currency earned only through play.

ONE PRICE. THE COMPLETE GAME.

Everything here is included in one purchase and earned through play.

No microtransactions, paid currency, card packs, paid battle pass, loot boxes, real-money wagering, or cash-out.

SHARED RULES. YOUR DECISIONS.

  • Every run is deterministic; share a BREACH CODE to replay its route.

BUILT FOR THE WHOLE RUN

  • Separate audio, display, atmosphere, post FX, shake, impact, and reduced-motion settings.

  • Card inspection, forecasts, reactive music, cinematics, hit-stop, shield fractures, kill dissolves, particles, and atmosphere.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE THE LEVEL

You are a drop of living ink, and everywhere you go, you leave a line. Not a pretty trail effect — a wall. Solid, permanent, and entirely your fault.

Jump a gap and you've drawn a ramp you can land on later. Fall down a shaft and you've split the room in two. Grab that shiny collectible without thinking, and congratulations: you've inked yourself into a corner with no way out. In DEADLINE, every level is solvable — but only if you plan your entire path like a single, continuous pen stroke.

DRAW YOUR WAY OUT

  • Your past is the architecture. Land on your own arcs, wall-jump off your own mistakes, knit ladders out of your falls.

  • One gap in the stroke. The Pen Lift lets you dash without drawing — once. Where you choose not to leave a mark is the whole puzzle.

  • Think first, execute second. Deaths teach routing, not reflexes. When you fail, it won't be your thumbs — it'll be that beautiful prison you built for yourself.

BEWARE THE RED PEN

The page fights back. Crosshatched spikes, strike-through lines, and stamped X's — every hazard is an editor's correction mark, and the Red Pen itself hunts anything that colors outside the lines. Solvent pools dissolve your ink. Fresh pages wipe the slate. Use them, or drown in your own handwriting.

ELEGANCE IS THE HIGH SCORE

You're not graded on speed. You're graded on ink. Every level scores your total stroke length — the shortest, cleanest line takes the gold. Finish a level and see your entire run framed as a single drawing: your solution, signed and hung on the wall. No two players draw the same picture.

  • 30+ hand-inked levels across notebook, graph paper, and aged parchment

  • A stroke-length medal system that rewards elegance over reflexes

  • Instant restarts, single-screen puzzles, zero filler

  • A living pen-on-paper art style where the whole world is hand-drawn — including by you

Solve it like a puzzle. Execute it like a speedrun. Frame it like art.

store_data.about_the_game:
Aircraft Tycoon is a strategy and management simulation game where you build and grow an aircraft manufacturing company from the pioneering age of aviation.

Begin with a small operation, limited resources, and early technology. Design aircraft, build prototypes, conduct tests, present your models to the market, and turn commercial opportunities into real orders.

BUILD YOUR AIRCRAFT COMPANY

Start with a modest worksite and gradually expand your company’s capabilities. Manage facilities, finances, aircraft models, contracts, suppliers, and production capacity.

DESIGN AND DEVELOP AIRCRAFT

Create aircraft by combining airframes, wings, engines, flight control systems, fuel systems, equipment packages, and landing gear.

Every decision affects performance, cost, reliability, safety, production difficulty, and how well the aircraft meets the needs of the market.

BUILD AND TEST PROTOTYPES

Turn your designs into working prototypes. Conduct ground tests, complete the first flight, and run flight test campaigns to identify technical limitations and validate each aircraft model.

Choose whether to correct problems, accept limitations, invest in further development, or redesign the aircraft.

PRESENT YOUR AIRCRAFT TO THE MARKET

Organize market demonstrations, attract potential customers, and evaluate commercial interest in your aircraft.

Different customers value different qualities, including price, reliability, performance, delivery time, and operational suitability.

NEGOTIATE ORDERS AND MANAGE CONTRACTS

Respond to commercial enquiries and define prices, quantities, and delivery schedules.

Promising more than your company can deliver may win an order in the short term, but delays and failures can damage your finances, customer relationships, and reputation.

SOURCE ENGINES AND MANAGE SUPPLIERS

Purchase engines from external suppliers, compare available offers, place priority orders, track deliveries, and manage engine inventory across your worksites.

Supplier availability, prices, and delivery times can directly affect aircraft design and production planning.

MANAGE PRODUCTION AND DELIVERY

Prepare production, allocate capacity, control costs, and manufacture aircraft for active contracts.

Successful deliveries generate revenue and strengthen your reputation. Poor planning, shortages, or unrealistic deadlines can threaten both the contract and the future of the company.

BUILD A COMPANY THAT CAN SURVIVE THE HISTORY OF AVIATION

Aircraft Tycoon is not a flight simulator. It is a business and industrial management game about technology, risk, markets, production, finance, and the long-term decisions required to build a successful aircraft manufacturer.

store_data.about_the_game:
LEAD · EXPLORE · CRAFT · BUILD · RESEARCH · TRADE · FIGHT

At the dawn of civilization, there are no safe borders, no roads to follow, and no future you can take for granted. There is only a small tribe, an uncharted land, and a leader whose choices will shape the fate of generations.

Stone to Stars is a colony sim and ruler simulator set at the dawn of civilization. Settle an uncharted continent, build a thriving settlement, discover new technologies, trade or wage war with your neighbors—and hold on to power as you guide your dynasty through the ages.

LEAD

You do not rule over a faceless colony, but a living society. Your people will follow you only as long as they trust your judgment and believe you can safeguard their future.

Endure crises, meet the needs of your tribe, and maintain the support of your people. Lose their trust, and you may be overthrown—and defeated.

But even the most successful reign must eventually end. Guide your dynasty, prepare worthy successors, and pass power into their hands so that what you began may endure for generations.

EXPLORE

At the start of each game, choose the continent on which your civilization’s story will unfold. Every continent has its own landscapes, climate, resources, and neighboring settlements.

Send your people into the unknown, reveal the map, locate sources of food and raw materials, choose where to expand, and discover who else lays claim to these lands.

CRAFT

Gather resources, hunt wildlife, process what you bring home, and turn natural materials into tools, weapons, clothing, and supplies.

Resources are not abstract numbers: they must be gathered, processed, carried, stored, and delivered wherever they are needed. Every item becomes part of your settlement’s physical economy.

BUILD

Begin with a single campfire and temporary shelters, then transform your settlement into a thriving state with homes, workshops, storehouses, farmland, and infrastructure.

Assign workers, organize logistics, and establish production chains. Resources will not move on their own, and every decision has consequences.

RESEARCH

Accumulate knowledge and choose your path of development. A branching technology tree unlocks new materials, crafts, gathering methods, buildings, and ways to organize your society.

Lead your people from the first stone tools into new eras. Every discovery reshapes life in your settlement and opens new possibilities for your civilization.

TRADE OR FIGHT

You are not alone on your chosen continent. Other settlements are autonomous, AI-controlled societies. They grow, explore the land, gather resources, and pursue goals of their own.

Exchange goods, cooperate, and preserve the peace—or exert pressure, defend your territory, and go to war. Relationships are shaped by your actions, so today’s trading partner may become tomorrow’s enemy.

FACE THE FINAL TRIAL

The growth of your civilization is not the only goal. Hidden within every game is an inevitable final trial that will demand everything your people have achieved across the generations.

Your accumulated knowledge, stockpiles, production chains, relationships with neighboring societies, and the consequences of generations of decisions will all shape the final struggle for the future. Only a civilization that has prepared for what lies ahead will be able to save its people and carry their story beyond the world they have always known.

Only then will you discover whether you have built a civilization capable of enduring through the ages—or one destined to vanish alongside all the rest.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dungeons and Dumbasses is a cooperative comedy dungeon crawler where up to four questionably qualified adventurers stumble through hand-crafted dimensions filled with monsters, puzzles, traps, and countless opportunities to sabotage each other.

Choose from four distinct classes - Knight, Archer, Wizard and Alchemist, each with unique abilities, weapons, and team roles. Rain fireballs from a safe distance, turn someone into a sheep with a polymorph potion, or completely miss your parry and get launched into a pit.

Unlock new weapons, potions, spells and arrows that make each playthrough different. Combine abilities to solve puzzles and take down monsters, and attempt to look competent while everything around you falls apart.

Traverse through different environments and take down the evils that plague the land.

Comes across never before seen monsters. The dungeon is dangerous. Your friends are dumbasses.
